Mikio Kaku, born on January 24, 1947, is an American scientist who explains physics. He teaches theoretical physics at City College of New York and CUNY Graduate Center. Kaku writes books and gives talks on physics. His popular science books include "Physics of the Impossible" (2008), "Physics of the Future" (2011), and "The Future of the Mind" (2014). He also appears on TV channels like BBC, Discovery, History, and Science.

Manuel Luis Quezon y Molina (August 19, 1878 – August 1, 1944), known as MLQ, was a Filipino statesman, soldier, and politician. He served as the president of the Philippines from 1935 to 1944. Quezon was the first Filipino to lead the whole country, after previous Philippine governments. He is often seen as the second president of the Philippines, following Emilio Aguinaldo. During his presidency, Quezon focused on helping poor farmers who had no land. Other big decisions he made included organizing the military defense, changing how the government worked, promoting settlement and development in Mindanao, dealing with foreign control over Philippine trade, suggesting land reform, and fighting corruption in the government. He set up a government-in-exile in the United States when World War II began and Japan threatened to invade. Quezon died of tuberculosis in New York and was buried at Arlington National Cemetery until after World War II ended. His final resting place is now the Quezon Memorial Circle. In 2015, President Benigno Aquino III and Maria Zenaida Quezon Avanceña, MLQ's daughter, learned that he had been given a special award posthumously by the International Raoul Wallenberg Foundation for helping people during the Holocaust between 1937 and 1941.

Ellen Louise Axson Wilson (born May 15, 1860; died August 6, 1914) was Woodrow Wilson's first wife and the mother of their three daughters. Like her husband, she came from the South and had a minister as her father. She was born in Savannah, Georgia, but grew up in Rome, Georgia. She liked art and studied at the Art Students League in New York before she married. After that, she kept making art. From 1913 until she died in 1914, she was known as the First Lady of the United States. During this time, she helped organize weddings for two of their daughters in the White House.

Hudson Hawk is an action-comedy movie from 1991, directed by Michael Lehmann. Bruce Willis stars as the main character and also wrote the story and theme song. Danny Aiello, Andie MacDowell, James Coburn, David Caruso, Lorraine Toussaint, Frank Stallone, Sandra Bernhard, and Richard E. Grant are in the film. The movie uses a lot of cartoon-style funny scenes with sound effects to make it more silly. It mixes ideas from conspiracy theories, secret groups, and old mysteries with made-up technology like clocks and gears. A funny part is that Hudson and his friend Tommy sing songs together but separately to help them work better. The movie features duets of "Swinging on a Star" by Bing Crosby and "Side by Side" by Paul Anka in the soundtrack. The film did not do well in the United States, earning only $17 million and getting three Razzie awards, including worst picture. But it was more popular overseas, making $80 million, for a total of $97 million worldwide.

The Katiti Aboriginal Land Trust, or KALT, is a land trust for an area in Petermann, near Australia's Northern Territory. It was created in 1980 through the Katiti Land Claim. The people who own this land are Pitjantjatjara, Yankunytjatjara, and Luritja. This land is officially called Northern Territory portion 1818. To its north and west lies the Uluṟu–Kata Tjuṯa National Park. To the east and south are two pastoral stations named Curtin Springs and Mulga Park. The town of Yulara is not part of this trust, but it's between the Katiti land and the national park. The trust is called after Katiti, also known as "Bobbie's Well," a natural spring located near Lake Amadeus. Baldwin Spencer and Francis James Gillen wrote about it in 1894 during their trip to Uluṟu. In 1903, Lawrence Wells' prospecting team visited the spring, and Herbert Basedow marked it as "Curtyteena" on his maps.

Princeton is a city in Mercer County, West Virginia, United States. It's called the "jewel of the south" or the "heart of Mercer County." According to the 2010 census, Princeton had 6,432 people. It's part of the Bluefield, WV-VA micropolitan area with a population of 107,342. Princeton hosts the Princeton Rays baseball club in the Appalachian League.

Raymond Poulidor, nicknamed "Pou-Pou," was a French professional racing cyclist born on April 15, 1936, and died on November 13, 2019. He rode as a professional his entire career. Although he competed against great cyclists like Jacques Anquetil and Eddy Merckx during his time, Poulidor was still famous for being an underdog. The public liked him because of this. People called him "the eternal second" because he never won the Tour de France but finished in second place three times and third place five times, including when he was 40 years old. Despite not wearing the yellow jersey as race leader, Poulidor completed 12 out of 14 Tours. He did win one big cycling race—the 1964 Vuelta a España.

The Bridgeport Sound Tigers are a professional ice hockey team. They play in the American Hockey League (AHL). The New York Islanders of the National Hockey League own them and have an AHL affiliation with the team. The Sound Tigers started playing in 2001-02. The NY Islanders bought the team in 2004. The team is from Bridgeport, Connecticut and plays its home games at Webster Bank Arena.

Gopinath Pandurang Munde, born on December 12, 1949, and passed away on June 3, 2014, was an Indian politician from Maharashtra. He was a well-known leader there called "lokneta." Munde belonged to the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and served as a senior leader. In Narendra Modi's government, he was the Union Minister for Rural Development and Panchayati Raj but held this position for only a short time because of his death in a road accident. He was elected to Maharashtra's Legislative Assembly (MLA) five times between 1980-1985 and 1990-2009. During 1992-1995, he led the opposition in the assembly. Munde also served as Deputy Chief Minister of Maharashtra from 1995 to 1999. He was elected to Lok Sabha twice—in 2009 and 2014—and became the deputy leader of BJP there. Munde joined Modi's cabinet on May 26, 2014, but unfortunately died a week later in New Delhi due to a road accident, making him the shortest-serving cabinet minister in India's history. Reports suggest he might have been murdered instead of dying in an accident, as claimed by a US hacker on January 21, 2019.

Mazdak was an Iranian priest and reformer who lived around 524 or 528. He was a Zoroastrian "mobad." During the rule of Sasanian Emperor Kavadh I, he gained influence. Mazdak claimed to be a prophet of Ahura Mazda and started programs to help people. Some see him as an early form of socialist.
Saul Asael Martínez Álvarez, born on January 29, 1976, is a Honduran football player. He plays as a forward for Miami United, which is in the fourth tier of American soccer.
The name Ana has been used for seven tropical cyclones in the Atlantic Ocean and one in the Central Pacific.

Margaret Higgins Sanger, born Margaret Louise Higgins on September 14, 1879, passed away on September 6, 1966, also known as Margaret Sanger Slee. She was an American who fought for birth control and education about sex. She popularized the term "birth control," opened the first birth control clinic in the United States, and helped start Planned Parenthood. Sanger used writing and speeches to share her ideas. In 1914, she was in trouble because of her book "Family Limitation." She went to Britain for a while until it was safe to return home. Her work led to legal changes that allowed birth control in the U.S. People who oppose abortion often criticize Sanger, but she made clear that she saw birth control and abortion as different things. Sanger believed women should have more equal roles in society and wanted them to live healthier lives by controlling when they had children. She also wanted to stop dangerous back-alley abortions, which were common because abortion was illegal at the time. Sanger opened the first U.S. birth control clinic in 1916 and got arrested for distributing information on contraception. Her trial caused a lot of discussion. In 1921, she created the American Birth Control League, now known as Planned Parenthood Federation of America. In New York City, she started clinics with female doctors and an African-American advisory council. From 1952 to 1959, Sanger was president of the International Planned Parenthood Federation. Sanger died in 1966 but is remembered as a key figure in the birth control movement.

Ștefan Andrei, born on March 29, 1931, and died on August 31, 2014, was a Romanian politician. He worked as the minister of foreign affairs in Romania from 1978 to 1985. After Nicolae Ceaușescu's government ended in 1989, Andrei was arrested.

Santa Rosa is a city in Guadalupe County, New Mexico, United States. In 2010, it had 2,848 people. It is between Albuquerque and Tucumcari. Santa Rosa sits by the Pecos River where Interstate 40, U.S. Route 54, and U.S. Route 84 meet. The city is on the western edge of the Llano Estacado, also known as the "staked plains," in eastern New Mexico and west Texas.
Here is a list of Guinea's presidents since it became independent from France in 1958, after voters said no to joining the French community.

Grandview Heights is a city in Franklin County, Ohio, United States. The population was 6,536 as of 2010. Originally part of Marble Cliff, one of Columbus's first suburbs, it settled as a community in 1890 and became the "hamlet of Marble Cliff" in 1901. Grandview Heights became a separate village in 1906 and a city in 1931. It has its own police and fire departments and runs its own school district. Its neighbor, Marble Cliff, uses services from Grandview Heights for its residents.
Hohentannen is a village in Weinfelden area, which is part of Thurgau in Switzerland.

Mark Alan Webber, born August 27, 1976, is an Australian former professional racing driver. He won the FIA World Endurance Championship in 2015 while driving for Porsche. Webber has nine Formula One race wins and finished third in the championship a few times. Before moving to the UK in 1995, he raced in Australia in Formula Ford and Holden races. In the UK, Webber worked with Paul Stoddart, who owned an F3000 racing team. They later bought the Minardi team for Formula One. In 2000, Webber beat Fernando Alonso, who was then 19, in the International Formula 3000 season. Webber made his Formula One debut with Minardi and scored the team's first points in three years at home. Jaguar chose him as their main driver after one season. Despite the team usually not doing well, Webber often started near the front of the race. His first win came at the 2009 German Grand Prix, following several second-place finishes. By 2010, he had eight podiums, including another victory in Brazil. In 2010 and 2011, he scored ten more podiums, with wins in Spain, Monaco, Britain, and Hungary. Webber finished third in the 2010 season, losing to teammate Sebastian Vettel. He won again in the 2011 Brazilian Grand Prix but was still third behind Vettel and Jenson Button. In 2011, he had no wins after two victories in Monaco and Britain, though his last win. Webber also worked for a long time with the Grand Prix Drivers' Association, which is like a union for Formula One drivers. In June 2013, Webber said he would retire from Formula One at the end of that season. He started racing for Porsche in 2014, competing in LMP1 sports cars in the FIA World Endurance Championship. Webber was one of six drivers of the Porsche 919 hybrid. In November 2015, he became world champion with Timo Bernhard and Brendon Hartley driving car #17. He later drove car #1 for a year. After retiring from racing, Webber worked as an occasional commentator for BBC's Formula One coverage in 2014-2015 and full-time for Channel 4's UK coverage in 2016. On October 13, 2016, he announced his retirement to focus on roles with Porsche and media work for Channel 4's F1 and WEC coverage.

extratropical cyclones, also known as mid-latitude or wave cyclones, are low-pressure systems that influence much of the earth's weather. Along with high-pressure anticyclones, they shape the weather in middle latitudes. These cyclones can create various conditions, such as clouds, light rain, strong winds, thunderstorms, heavy snow, and even tornadoes. Extratropical cyclones are large-scale low-pressure systems found in mid-latitudes. Unlike tropical cyclones, they cause quick changes in temperature and dew point around the center of the cyclone, along lines called weather fronts.

Matthew Nagy, born on April 24, 1978, is an American football coach and former quarterback who plays in the Arena Football League. Currently, he coaches the Chicago Bears in the National Football League (NFL). As a quarterback, he played college football for the University of Delaware from 1997 to 2000. He set various school passing records during his time there. After not getting an NFL contract, Nagy joined the Arena Football League. He played for four teams: the New York Dragons, Carolina Cobras, Georgia Force, and Columbus Destroyers over six seasons. Nagy started as an assistant coach with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2009 under head coach Andy Reid. He worked on offensive positions for five years. In 2013, when Andy Reid moved to the Kansas City Chiefs, Nagy followed him as the quarterbacks coach. He held this position until he became the offensive coordinator in 2016. Nagy was named head coach of the Chicago Bears in 2018. In his first year, he led the team to their first NFC North championship and a playoff appearance since 2010.

Potosí is a department in southwestern Bolivia. It has an area of 118,218 square kilometers and around 823,517 people (as of the 2012 census). The capital city is Potosí. Most of the region is dry and mountainous. To the west, there is a large plateau where you can find the Salar de Uyuni, which is the world's largest salt flat. Potosí used to be one of the richest areas in the Spanish Empire because it produced a lot of silver that was sent to Europe. Today, it has mines for silver, zinc, and lead. These mines were developed by Apex Silver Mines Limited from Colorado. In November 2008, they were sold to Sumitomo Corporation, a Japanese company.

The Great Atlantic Hurricane in 1944 was a very strong tropical storm that hit parts of the U.S. East Coast in September. It caused the most damage in New England but also affected areas like the Outer Banks, Mid-Atlantic states, and Canada's Maritimes. People compared it to the 1938 Long Island Express because both were powerful storms in New England history. The storm started as a disturbance east of the Lesser Antilles on September 4. It became a tropical cyclone northeast of the Virgin Islands on September 9. The storm moved west-northwest and grew stronger, reaching its strongest point north of the Bahamas on September 13 after turning north. On September 14, it passed by the Outer Banks and hit Long Island and Rhode Island as a weaker hurricane on September 15. After that, the storm changed into an extratropical cyclone and continued moving northeast. It merged with another system off Greenland on September 16.

Mostafa Pour-Mohammadi, born on March 9, 1960, in Qom, Iran, is a politician and prosecutor. He held important positions, including minister of interior from 2005 to 2008, and minister of justice from 2013 until 2017. Pour-Mohammadi is said to be involved in the 1988 massacre of Iranian prisoners.
Sarat Pujari was born on August 8, 1934, and passed away on May 12, 2014. He was an actor, director, and producer in Odia films. He came from a place called Jhaduapada in Sambalpur.

John Dixon was born on February 20, 1929, and died on May 7, 2015. He was an Australian comic book artist and writer. John is famous for creating a comic strip called "Air Hawk and the Flying Doctors," which lasted from 1959 to 1986.

Wind energy is using the wind to make electricity through wind turbines, which can also do other work like grinding grains or pumping water. It’s a clean and renewable source with less environmental impact than burning fossil fuels. Wind farms have many individual wind turbines connected to an electric network. Onshore wind power is cheap and competitive, sometimes even cheaper than coal or gas plants. However, it changes the landscape because it requires more land spread over wild areas, potentially leading to countryside industrialization and habitat loss. Offshore wind has stronger and steadier winds but costs more to build and maintain. It’s less visible from shore but harder to fix. Small onshore farms can feed some energy into the grid or supply remote locations with electricity. Wind is an unpredictable source of power that cannot be used when needed. Its output varies a lot, making it hard to rely solely on wind for electricity. As more wind farms are built, traditional power sources are needed as backup, and sometimes the electric grid needs upgrades. Techniques like using other power sources when wind isn't enough, having extra hydroelectric capacity, spreading turbines across different areas, or storing energy can help solve these issues. Accurate weather forecasting also helps manage production changes. In 2018, wind provided about 4.8% of the world's electricity, and by then, global wind power was reaching 591 gigawatts. In Europe, it supplied around 15% of consumed electricity in 2019. Many countries now use wind to generate their electricity.

The Belize Barrier Reef runs along the coast of Belize, both north and south within the country. It is part of a large system called the Mesoamerican Barrier Reef, which stretches from Cancún in Mexico to Honduras. This makes it the second-largest coral reef system after Australia's Great Barrier Reef. It's very popular for scuba diving and snorkeling; almost half of Belize’s 260,000 visitors come here each year. The reef is also important for fishing. In 1842, Charles Darwin called it "the most remarkable reef in the West Indies." Besides the barrier reef, there are three Caribbean atolls: Turneffe Atoll, Glover's Reef, and Lighthouse Reef. The Wiener Sport-Club, sometimes abbreviated as WSC, was founded in 1883 in Vienna, Austria. It is one of the oldest sports clubs in the country. Their main location is in the Dornbach area (17th district) of the city.

County Armagh is named after its main town, Armagh. It is one of Ireland's traditional counties and part of Northern Ireland, made up of six counties. Situated near Lough Neagh, County Armagh covers 1,326 square kilometers and has about 174,792 people living there. County Armagh is called the "Orchard County" because it has many apple orchards. It belongs to a historic area known as Ulster.

Portage la Prairie is a small city in Manitoba, Canada. In 2016, it had 13,304 people living there. The city is located in the central part of the plains region. It's about west of Winnipeg along the Trans-Canada Highway. This highway is between Saskatchewan and Ontario borders. Portage la Prairie sits next to the Assiniboine River, which used to flood the town often until a channel was built to direct floodwaters north to Lake Manitoba. The city is surrounded by the Rural Municipality of Portage la Prairie. Environment Canada says it has the most sunny days during warm months in all of Canada. It's also where the Dakota Tipi First Nations reserve is based.

Khunjerab Pass is a high mountain pass located in the Karakoram Mountains. It sits on Pakistan's northern border, specifically in Gilgit-Baltistan's Hunza and Nagar districts. The pass also marks part of Pakistan's southwestern border with China's Xinjiang region. Its exact height is not stated here.

In cellular biology, active transport moves molecules across a cell membrane. It goes from an area with fewer molecules to an area with more—against the concentration gradient. This process needs energy from the cell. There are two kinds: primary active transport uses ATP for energy; secondary active transport relies on an electrochemical gradient. An example in the human body is how glucose is absorbed in the intestines.
The Akryrios is a tragedy written by Sophocles, an Athenian playwright from the 5th century BCE. Only parts of it remain today.

The Fulbright Program helps people from different countries learn and work together. It includes the Fulbright-Hays Program and other U.S. cultural exchange programs. The goal is to improve understanding between Americans and citizens of other countries by exchanging students, knowledge, and skills. Through this program, selected American citizens like students, teachers, professionals, scientists, and artists can travel abroad to study or teach. They can also do research or show their talents. Similarly, people from other countries can come to the United States for the same purposes. The Fulbright Program was started in 1946 by U.S. Senator J. William Fulbright and is one of the most well-known scholarships globally. About 8,000 grants are given each year. This includes about 1,600 for American students, 1,200 for American scholars, 4,000 for foreign students, 900 for foreign visiting scholars, and several hundred for teachers and professionals. The program is run by groups like the Institute of International Education in over 160 countries. It gets money from the U.S. Department of State's Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, which also receives funding from Congress each year. Other support comes from governments, foundations, corporations, and local institutions both inside and outside the United States. In 49 countries, a Fulbright Commission works together with the program. In other countries, the U.S. embassy helps manage it. Over 370,000 people have taken part in the program since its start. Many of them have won important prizes like Nobel and Pulitzer awards.

The first United States Congress started in March 1789 and ended in March 1791. It met first at Federal Hall in New York City, then moved to Congress Hall in Philadelphia. This happened during George Washington's presidency. The U.S. government began officially operating under the new Constitution that was formed in 1787. The House of Representatives had seats based on what the Constitution said. Both the Senate and House mostly supported the president. This Congress sent twelve proposed changes to the Constitution to the states. Ten of these were accepted by the states and became part of the Constitution, known as the Bill of Rights, in 1791.

Sabayon Linux, also called Sabayon, is a Gentoo-based Italian Linux distribution created by Fabio Erculiani and the Sabayon development team. It has many applications ready for use right away and sets up itself automatically. Sabayon uses a rolling release cycle with its own software repository and package management system named Entropy. You can choose from both x86 and AMD64 versions of Sabayon Linux, and they are working on making it available for ARMv7 devices like the BeagleBone. The name Sabayon comes from an Italian dessert called zabaione, which is made with eggs. The logo shows a chicken's foot.
Patrick Barnabas Burke Mayhew, also known as Baron Mayhew of Twysden, was born on September 11, 1929, and died on June 25, 2016. He was a British lawyer and politician.

Conficker is a computer worm targeting Microsoft Windows that first appeared in November 2008. It spreads by using vulnerabilities in the Windows operating system and guessing passwords through dictionaries. Conficker also creates a botnet, making it hard to control because of its use of advanced malware techniques. This worm infected millions of computers worldwide, affecting government, business, and home machines in over 190 countries. It is considered one of the largest known computer worm infections since the 2003 Welchia incident. The worm didn't cause much damage, possibly due to the cautious behavior of its believed Ukrainian creators. Four men were arrested, with one admitting guilt and receiving a 48-month prison sentence.

seattle sounders fc is an American soccer team in Seattle, Washington. They are part of Major League Soccer (MLS) in the Western Conference. The club started in 2007 and first played in 2009 as a new MLS team. Their name comes from an earlier team that existed between 1974 and 1983. Adrian Hanauer is the main owner, with other owners including Paul Allen's family, Drew Carey, and 11 Seattle families. In July 2016, Brian Schmetzer became their coach after Siggi Schmid left. They play at CenturyLink Field, which has about 37, 722 seats for most games. A band called Sound Wave supports them at home matches. The team plays against nearby rivals Portland Timbers and Vancouver Whitecaps FC to win the Cascadia Cup. Their first game was on March 19, 2009, when they won 3-0 against the New York Red Bulls. Seattle is very successful in MLS, winning four U.S. Open Cups, the Supporters' Shield in 2014, and the MLS Cup twice in 2016 and 2019. They have been in playoffs every year since they started and played in the Concacaf Champions League five times, reaching the semifinals once. The team has a lot of fans because their average attendance was high for five years straight. They are also one of the most valuable teams in North America. Their players include Clint Dempsey and Fredy Montero as top goal scorers, Osvaldo Alonso as a long-time captain, and Nicolás Lodeiro as current captain. The team has a player academy that produces homegrown talent like Jordan Morris and DeAndre Yedlin, who now plays for Newcastle United.

negligence is failing to take proper care. In legal terms, it means not being careful enough when you should be. This happens when someone does something careless or doesn't do what they're supposed to in certain situations. In the part of law called tort law, negligence involves causing harm by not acting carefully. It can happen even if there were special circumstances that made it harder to act properly. The main idea is that people should be careful and consider potential harm when their actions could affect others or things. If someone gets hurt because another person was negligent, they might sue for compensation to make up for the loss. This loss could mean physical injury, damage to property, mental health problems, or financial loss. To understand negligence laws, you can think of it in five parts: first, there's a duty to be careful; second, if someone doesn't do that; third, their actions must have caused the harm; fourth, this harm should be considered close enough to the action; and finally, there needs to be damages or loss.

Troup County (pronounced) is in the middle part of Georgia, U.S. In 2010, it had about 67,044 people. The main town is Lagrange. Troup County is part of the Lagrange, GA micropolitan area and is included in the Atlanta-Athens-Clarke County-Sandy Springs, GA combined statistical area.

A creed, often called a confession or statement of faith, is a formal summary of shared beliefs in a community. One early Christian creed was "Jesus is Lord," first mentioned by Saint Paul. The Nicene Creed, used by many Christians today, was created in 325 AD at the First Council of Nicaea. It describes the idea of the Trinity and is seen as important for most Christian groups. Another widely accepted creed is the Apostles' Creed. Some Christian groups do not follow these creeds. Muslims declare a statement called the Shahada: "I believe in one God, and Muhammad is His messenger." Whether or not Judaism has a creed is debated. Some think Judaism doesn't have formal beliefs everyone must agree with. Others say it has a key belief, the Shema: "Hear O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One."

"Dexter in the Dark" is a 2007 novel by Jeff Lindsay. It's the third book in the Dexter series. The first book, "Darkly Dreaming Dexter," came out in 2004 and was made into a TV show on Showtime. A second book, "Dearly Devoted Dexter," followed in 2005. "Dexter in the Dark" was released on September 18, 2007, in the U.S., and October 3, 2007, in the U.K. It originally had an earlier release date. The first two chapters of this book are available when you watch Season 1 DVDs of the TV series on a computer.

Jorge Zavala Baquerizo was born on May 13, 1921, and passed away on May 9, 2014. He was an Ecuadorian politician. Zavala worked as the vice president of Ecuador from 1968 to 1970 during José María Velasco Ibarra's government. He also served as the president of the National Congress from 1987 to 1988. Zavala was part of the Democratic Left party. He died in Guayaquil, Ecuador, due to natural causes at the age of 92.

The new year is when a new calendar year starts, often celebrated with holidays. In most places, January 1st marks this event. This was also the first day in the old Roman calendar after 153 BC and Julian calendar. During the Middle Ages in Europe, different days were used for New Year's Day depending on where you lived, like March 25th or Easter. After 1582, many places adopted January 1st as New Year’s Day with the Gregorian calendar. Other cultures have their own traditional new years, such as Chinese New Year, Islamic New Year, Japanese New Year, and Jewish New Year. In India and some other countries, multiple dates for celebrating the new year exist.

Romain Rolland, born on January 29, 1866, and died on December 30, 1944, was a French writer and thinker. He wrote plays, novels, essays, and books about art. In 1915, he won the Nobel Prize for Literature because his works were idealistic and showed different types of people with truth and sympathy. Rolland supported Stalin in France. He also had important conversations with Freud, influencing him.
Caucasian refers to: White people.

A railway brake is a device used on train cars to slow down, control speed going downhill, or keep them stationary when stopped. It works similarly to brakes on regular cars, but with added complexity needed for managing multiple linked carriages and ensuring effectiveness even without a running engine. Clasp brakes are an example of one type of brake historically used on trains.

In creation myths, 'five suns' refers to the belief held by the Aztecs and other Nahua peoples that our world came after four previous worlds. These earlier worlds were created but destroyed by gods. The current world is called the fifth sun. The Aztecs saw themselves as "people of the sun." They believed they had a duty to fight in cosmic wars to give the sun what it needed—blood and hearts. Without this, the sun might disappear. So, the survival of the universe depends on these offerings.

Uranium-235, or U, is an isotope found in about 0.72% of natural uranium. Unlike the most common isotope, uranium-238, it can sustain a fission chain reaction and is the only naturally occurring fissile isotope. It has a half-life of 703.8 million years. Uranium-235 was discovered in 1935 by Arthur Jeffrey Dempster. Uranium-235 can absorb slow neutrons and split into smaller parts, called fission. For slow neutrons, its ability to do this is about 584.3 barns. With fast neutrons, it's much less, around 1 barn. Most of the time when uranium-235 absorbs a neutron, it splits. Sometimes, though, it captures the neutron without splitting.
Deer Park is a city in Hamilton County, Ohio, United States. It is a suburb of Cincinnati. According to the 2010 census, Deer Park had a population of 5,736 people.

Ronald Vaughan Joyce, born on October 19, 1930, and passed away on January 31, 2019, was a Canadian entrepreneur who became a billionaire. In 1964, he co-founded the Tim Hortons doughnut chain with Tim Horton as his partner and first franchisee. After Tim Horton's death, Ron Joyce helped set up the Tim Hortons Children's Camps and the Tim Hortons Children's Foundation. He received many awards for his business success and charity work. In 1992, he was named a member of the Order of Canada because of his dedication to helping poor children and young people.

Delphi (formerly also called Pytho) is an ancient sanctuary that became rich because it housed the oracle, known as the Pythia. People from all over the ancient world asked her for advice on important decisions. The ancient Greeks believed Mount Parnassus was the center of the world and marked it with a stone monument called the Omphalos (navel). Delphi is located on the southwestern slope of Mount Parnassus, overlooking the southern coast and the valley of Phocis. Today, it's an archaeological site with a small modern town nearby. UNESCO recognizes Delphi as a world heritage site due to its significant influence in ancient times. Many important Greek city-states built monuments there, showing their strong unity as Hellenes.
Helensburgh Football Club was a Scottish team in Helensburgh. They played in the Scottish Football League Third Division from 1923 to 1926.

Addison Mitchell McConnell Jr., born February 20, 1942, is an American politician. He serves as Kentucky's senior U.S. Senator and Senate Majority Leader. McConnell is the second Kentuckian to lead a senate party, and he has been the longest-serving U.S. senator from Kentucky and the longest-serving Republican leader in the U.S. Senate. McConnell first won his seat in 1984 and has been re-elected five times since. He was the National Republican Senatorial Committee chairman during the 1998 and 2000 election cycles. In 1998, he became Majority Whip and held this position until 2004. In 2006, McConnell became Senate Minority Leader until 2015 when Republicans gained control of the Senate. Then, he became Majority Leader. Early in his career, McConnell was seen as a pragmatist and moderate Republican but shifted to the right over time. He opposed stricter campaign finance laws, leading to a Supreme Court ruling that partially overturned the McCain-Feingold Act in 2010. During Barack Obama's presidency, McConnell tried to stop major initiatives by withholding support, often used filibusters, and blocked several of Obama's judicial nominees, including Merrick Garland for the Supreme Court. Under Donald Trump, McConnell led Senate Republicans who confirmed more judicial nominees than ever before. Neil Gorsuch and Brett Kavanaugh were among those confirmed to the Supreme Court.

The Teruel Cathedral, or Catedral de Santa María de Mediavilla de Teruel, is a Roman Catholic church in Teruel. It is dedicated to Saint Mary and shows Mudéjar architecture. This cathedral, along with other churches in the town and in Zaragoza province, became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1986.
Alfred, born around 902, was Edward the Elder's second son. He was born after Edward married Aelflaed for the second time. Alfred died on August 2, 924.
dastilbe was a type of prehistoric fish. It is now extinct. It lived in the Aptian period.

Badfinger were a rock band from Wales, formed in Swansea. They played music from the 1960s to the 1980s. Their main members were Pete Ham, Mike Gibbins, Tom Evans, and Joey Molland. The band started as another group called The Iveys in 1961. In 1968, they signed with Apple Records, which was run by the Beatles. They changed their name to Badfinger because of a Beatles song title. From 1968 to 1973, Badfinger made five albums and toured a lot. During this time, they had four big hits: "Come and Get It," "No Matter What," "Day After Day," and "Baby Blue." Their song "Without You" was also popular and later became a hit for other singers. After Apple Records closed in 1973, Badfinger faced many problems. Pete Ham died in 1975. The surviving members had legal troubles and tried to make more music but found it hard. In 1983, Tom Evans also passed away.

The Imja Khola is a small river in Nepal. It flows into the Dudh Koshi River. The Imja Khola comes from Mount Everest's slopes. The Khumbu Glacier melts and joins the Lobujya, which becomes the Imja Khola as it travels south. The Imja Khola meets the Dudh Kosi at a place called Tengboche. Some water also comes from the Imja Glacier through Dingboche Valley.

"Sunday Bloody Sunday" is a song by the Irish rock band U2. It's from their 1983 album "War" and came out as the third single in March 1983, first in the Netherlands and West Germany. The song has a strong drumbeat, loud guitar sounds, and pleasant melodies. One of U2's most political songs, its lyrics talk about feeling sad because of violence during the troubles in Northern Ireland, focusing on the Bloody Sunday incident in Derry where British soldiers killed unarmed protesters in 1972. Along with "New Year's Day," this song helped U2 become more popular. Critics liked it when the album was released. The song has often been played at U2 concerts since its early performances caused some controversy. U2’s singer, Bono, kept reminding his audience about the message against violence for many years. Today, "Sunday Bloody Sunday" is one of U2's most famous songs and is often performed live. Many people think it is a great political protest song. Over 10 other artists have covered this song. It was ranked as the 272nd-greatest song by Rolling Stone in their list of the top 500 songs of all time.

Fort Scott is a city in Kansas, United States. It's in Bourbon County and is near the Marmaton River. According to the 2010 census, Fort Scott has about 8,087 people living there. The city is known for two important places: Fort Scott National Historic Site and Fort Scott National Cemetery. The city is named after General Winfield Scott.

In 1965, "How to Murder Your Wife" was an American black comedy film from United Artists. George Axelrod produced it, Richard Quine directed it, and Jack Lemmon, Virna Lisi, and Terry-Thomas starred in it. Quine also directed Jack Lemmon in other films like "My Sister Eileen," "It Happened to Jane," "Operation Mad Ball," "The Notorious Landlady," and "Bell, Book and Candle." Mel Keefer drew the comic strip art featured in the film. He created newspaper comics such as "Perry Mason," "Mac Divot," and "Rick O'Shay." Alex Toth made a teaser comic strip in Keefer's style for ten days before the movie opened, running in "The Hollywood Reporter" and several newspapers.
Hiroshi Umemura, born on February 22, 1972, is from Japan. He is a fighter in mixed martial arts. He fought in both the bantamweight and featherweight categories.

Action Comics is an American comic book/magazine series that introduced Superman, a famous superhero. The company that published it was called National Allied Publications first, then changed to National Comics Publications and National Periodical Publications before becoming DC Comics. The original version of the comics ran from 1938 to 2011 and had issues numbered in sequence, making it one of the longest-running comic books. A second volume of Action Comics started with issue #1 in 2011 and ended in 2016. After that, the series returned to its original numbering starting from issue #957 in August 2016.
The Centre Étienne Desmarteau is a versatile building in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. It has two ice rinks.

Stephen Lewis, born on December 17, 1926, and passed away on August 12, 2015, was known as Stephen Cato early in his career. He worked as an actor, comedian, director, screenwriter, and playwright. People remember him most for playing Inspector Cyril "Blakey" Blake on a show called "The Buses." He also played Clem "Smiler" Hemmingway in "Last of the Summer Wine" and Harry Lambert in "Oh, Doctor Beeching!" Besides these roles, he acted in many stage and film productions.

In chemistry, a leaving group is a part of a molecule that goes away with an electron pair when a bond breaks. It can be an ion (like chloride, bromide, iodide, or sulfonate esters) or a neutral molecule (like water or ammonia). For the breaking to happen, it needs to stabilize extra electrons. Common ions that leave are halides such as chlorine, bromine, and iodine, and sulfonate esters like tosylate. Fluoride can also leave in some nerve agents. Neutral molecules that often leave include water and ammonia. Sometimes, positively charged parts of a molecule (like hydrogen released during benzene nitration) can act as leaving groups too. These are called electrofuges.

Caliban is the second-biggest irregular satellite that moves backward around Uranus. It was found on September 6, 1997, by Brett J. Gladman, Philip D. Nicholson, Joseph A. Burns, and John J. Kavelaars using a big telescope called the 200-inch Hale Telescope. At first, it had a temporary name, s/1997 U 1. Later, it was named Uranus XVI. This moon is called Caliban because it comes from a character in Shakespeare's play "The Tempest."

The German flag consists of three equal horizontal bands of black, red, and gold. It was first used as Germany's national flag in 1919 during the Weimar Republic until 1933. Since the mid-1800s, Germany has had two main sets of national colors: black-red-gold and black-white-red. Black-red-gold are the colors from the 1848 revolutions, the Weimar Republic (1919–1933), and the current federal republic (since 1949). The German Democratic Republic used these colors from 1949 to 1990 but added a socialist coat of arms in 1959. Black-white-red first appeared in 1867, during the North German Confederation, which included Prussia and other northern states. This state became known as the German Empire after including southern states from 1870–1871. It used these colors until 1918-1919. After that, black-white-red symbolized the political right. Nazi Germany revived these colors in 1933 along with their own swastika flag. After World War II, black-white-red was still used by some conservative groups or far-right groups because it is not forbidden like proper Nazi symbols. Black-red-gold is officially the flag of the Federal Republic of Germany. It is protected as an official symbol of the constitutional order, and according to German law, defaming it can result in a fine or up to five years in prison.

betrayal is the breaking or violation of a presumptive contract , trust , or confidence that produces moral and psychological conflict within a relationship amongst individuals , between organizations or between individuals and organizations . often betrayal is the act of supporting a rival group , or it is a complete break from previously decided upon or presumed norms by one party from the others . someone who betrays others is commonly called a traitor or betrayer . betrayal is also a commonly used literary element , also used in other fiction like films and tv series , and is often associated with or used as a plot twist .
Ile-d'Ale is a small town in Vendée, which is in Pays de la Loire. This region is located in western France.

Anna Kavan, born Helen Emily Woods on April 10, 1901, and passed away on December 5, 1968, was from Britain. She wrote novels and short stories and painted too. At first, she used the name Helen Ferguson for her publications. In 1939, she began using Anna Kavan as both a pen name and her legal name.

Hamont-Achel is a town in Belgium's Limburg province. It was formed in 1977 by combining the city Hamont and village Achel. On January 1, 2006, it had 13,770 people living there. The town covers 43. 66 square kilometers, making the population density about 315 people per square kilometer. It has an important Trappist abbey called Achel Abbey. Part of this abbey is a brewery named De Achelse Kluis, one of eleven Trappist breweries in the world. Professional tennis player Elise Mertens lives in Hamont-Achel.

In October 2015, an election took place to choose a new Speaker of the U.S. House of Representatives. This happened on October 29, during the 114th Congress. John Boehner, who was the previous Speaker, planned to resign on October 30. Boehner had been the first to step down in the middle of his term since 1989. This was the 124th election for a House Speaker since 1789. Paul Ryan, a Republican and chairman of the Ways and Means Committee, won with 236 votes. Nancy Pelosi, a Democrat and minority leader, got 184 votes, and others received 12 votes. To win, a candidate needed 217 votes. Paul Ryan was younger than any previous Speaker since James G. Blaine in 1869. After winning, Ryan gave his first speech as speaker-elect and was sworn in by John Conyers on October 30. Boehner had been Speaker since January 5, 2011. During his time, he faced many disputes with the Freedom Caucus. Before the election, Kevin McCarthy, who was House Majority Leader, seemed likely to win but withdrew when the Freedom Caucus refused to support him. The conference then voted for Paul Ryan after getting support from different party groups. On October 28, Ryan won the conference vote and became Speaker on October 29.
Hans-Peter Müller, known as Hansi, was born on July 27, 1957, in Stuttgart. He used to be a German football player and played as a midfielder.
St. Francis is a city in Clay County, Arkansas, United States. It is located near the St. Francis River. The city had 250 people living there according to the 2010 count.

jules henri poincaré (29 april 1854 – 17 july 1912) was a french mathematician, physicist, engineer, and philosopher. People say he was very talented in many fields of science and math. In mathematics, he was one of the last who could be an expert in all areas. poincaré made important contributions to math and physics. He worked on problems like the three-body problem and found a system that showed randomness in nature, which helped develop chaos theory. He is also seen as a founder of topology, a branch of math. in his work, poincaré noted how physical laws stay the same under different changes. He presented transformations called lorentz transformations in their modern form. Poincaré found more velocity transformations and wrote about them to lorentz in 1905. His work helped create special relativity theory. he also suggested gravitational waves exist, sending out from a body at light speed, needed for lorentz's theory. The poincaré group, used in physics and math, is named after him. early in the 20th century, he proposed what became known as the poincaré conjecture, an important unsolved problem in math until it was solved in 2002-2003 by grigori perelman.

Wellin is a Walloon municipality in Belgium, located in the province of Luxembourg. As of January 1, 2007, it had an area of 67.52 km² and 2,958 people living there. That means there were about 44 people per square kilometer. Wellin includes several smaller areas: Wellin itself, Chanly, Halma, Lomprez, and Sohier. Other towns nearby are Barzin, Froidlieu, Fays-Famenne, and Neupont.

Lynwood is a city in Los Angeles County, California. The population was 69,772 in the 2010 census, slightly down from 69,845 in 2000. Lynwood is close to South Gate and Compton in southern Los Angeles. It became an incorporated city in 1921. Lynwood is named after Lynn Wood Sessions, who was Charles Sessions' wife and a local dairy farmer. The nearby railroad station was also called Lynwood.
Trachselwald is a village in the Emmental region of the Swiss canton of Bern.

James Edward Westcott was an American photographer born on January 20, 1922, and died on March 29, 2019. He worked with the U.S. government in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, during the Manhattan Project and the Cold War. As one of few allowed to take photos there, he took many pictures of building and running the facilities at Oak Ridge and of everyday life for people living there.

Love and Basketball is a movie made in 2000. It is about romance and playing basketball. The film stars Sanaa Lathan and Omar Epps. In the story, Quincy McCalm, played by Epps, and Monica Wright, played by Lathan, are neighbors who both love basketball. They eventually fall in love. This movie was the first time Gina Prince-Bythewood directed a film. It came out on April 21, 2000, in the United States. People who watched it liked what they saw.

Like other games in the "Super Smash Bros." series, both "Super Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS" and "Super Smash Bros. for Wii U" are fighting games where players use different attacks to weaken their opponents and knock them out of an arena. These games include characters, items, music, and stages from various Nintendo franchises as well as some third-party ones. The development began in 2012 and was announced at E3 in 2013. The gameplay is balanced between the faster and more competitive "Super Smash Bros. Melee" and the slower and more casual-friendly "Super Smash Bros. Brawl." New features include up to eight players fighting together on the Wii U version, support for Nintendo's amiibo, using custom Miis as playable fighters, post-release downloadable content with new fighters and stages, and customizable special moves. Some features from previous games were removed, such as the story mode in "Brawl." Critics praised the fine-tuning of existing gameplay but had some issues with online play. Both versions sold well—over nine million copies for the 3DS version by December 2017, and over five million for the Wii U version during the same period. This game was followed by "Super Smash Bros. Ultimate" for Nintendo Switch in 2018.
guttert-Feschel is a town in the Leuk district, in the Valais canton, Switzerland. It became one town when Gutten and Feschel joined together in 2000.

Rafael Alkorta Martínez was born on September 16, 1968. He is a Spanish former footballer who mainly played as a central defender. Currently, he works as the sporting director for Athletic Bilbao. Alkorta played for Athletic Bilbao and Real Madrid during his 17-year professional career. He made 370 La Liga appearances and scored eight goals. He helped Real Madrid win three trophies. He also played three times for the Spanish national team in World Cups during the 1990s.
Ryland Heights is a city in Kentucky. It's in Kenton County and is part of the Cincinnati area. The number of people living there increased from 799 in 2000 to 1,022 in 2010.
Dorothea Sally Eilers was an American actress. She lived from December 11, 1908, to January 5, 1978.
Matthias Lukas Ginter, born on January 19, 1994, is a German soccer player. He plays as a center back for Borussia Mönchengladbach in the Bundesliga and also represents the Germany national team.

Diving Machine G5 is a roller coaster at Janfusun Fancyworld, in Taiwan. It was made by Swiss company Bolliger & Mabillard in 2000. Diving Machine G5 was the second Dive Coaster built; the first one was called Oblivion and was at Alton Towers in the United Kingdom. This roller coaster is in the Sky Plaza section of the park. It looks almost like Oblivion, its predecessor. The name "Diving Machine G5" comes from the strong g-forces felt during the drop. Like Insane Speed, Diving Machine G5 has no theme. Along with Ku Ku and Insane Speed, it is one of three roller coasters at the park. Because it's close to the entrance, this ride gets long lines in the morning but shorter waits later in the day.

James W. Hardy III (December 24, 1985 – June 7, 2017) was a wide receiver in American football. He was chosen by the Buffalo Bills in the second round of the 2008 NFL draft. Hardy also played for the Baltimore Ravens. He went to Indiana University to play college football.
Koenigsegg Automotive AB makes very fast and exciting sports cars. They are located in Ängelholm, Skåne County, Sweden.

Alfredo Félix Aльcóн was an Argentine actor born in Buenos Aires on March 3, 1930. He worked as a film and theatre actor for over five decades. His first movie was "Love Never Dies" in 1955. He received many awards during his career, including the Silver Condor, the Martin Fierro Award, and the 1981 Diamond Konex Award. Alfredo Félix Aльcóн passed away on April 11, 2014, at the age of 84.

Uzbekistan joined the Olympics as an independent country in 1994. Since then, Uzbek athletes have competed in every Olympic Games. Before that, Uzbek athletes took part in the Olympics as part of the Soviet Union from 1952 to 1988. After the Soviet Union ended, Uzbekistan was on a unified team in 1992. Uzbek athletes have won 26 medals in summer Olympics mostly in wrestling and boxing. They also got one medal in winter Olympics. The country's Olympic committee was formed in 1992 and recognized by the IOC in 1993.

Brendan Halligan was born on July 5, 1936, and passed away on August 9, 2020. He was an Irish economist and politician. Halligan founded and led the Institute of International and European Affairs (IIEA), a think tank that focuses on European and international issues. In addition, he was president of the Ireland China Institute, an independent think tank in Dublin, Ireland, which started officially in October 2019. His career included work in both Irish public sector organizations and the private sector. At different times, Halligan held several important positions: he was the general secretary of the Labour Party, a Teachta Dála (TD) in Ireland's parliament, a senator, and a member of the European Parliament (MEP).

Ofterchwang is a town in southern Germany, specifically in Oberallgäu, Bavaria. It hosts professional winter sports events like World Cup alpine races. The area is known for skiing and other sports. Traditionally, the region was agricultural. Ofterchwang has a church with a World War II memorial, as well as small chapels. Nowadays, tourism is important in this area. In winter, people come to ski. During summer, hiking, mountain biking, and parachute flying are popular activities. Tourists also enjoy "dorfsabend," which features traditional Bavarian costumes, dancing, food, and beer.

The Cheongyang chili pepper, also called dang jo cheongyang, is a medium-sized variety of the capsicum annuum species. It has a heat level of 10,000 Scoville units. These peppers look like regular Korean chili peppers but are much spicier. Cheongyang chili peppers come from Cheongyang County in South Korea. However, they were developed by Dr. Yoo Il-Woong. He used local Jeju Island chilli and Thai chilli to create them. When young, the peppers can be light purple or green. As they ripen, they turn a deep red color. Even when dried, these peppers stay dark red.
grimbosq is a town in Calvados. Calvados is in Normandy, which is in western France.

Saliva, also called spit, is a fluid produced by the salivary glands in your mouth. In humans, it's mostly water but also contains electrolytes, mucus, white blood cells, and enzymes like amylase and lipase that help break down food. Saliva includes antimicrobial agents such as secretory IgA and lysozymes. These enzymes start breaking down the starches and fats from your food during digestion. They also clean food particles stuck between teeth, protecting them from bacteria. Saliva helps by making food wet so you can swallow it easily and keeps your mouth moist. Different animals use their saliva in unique ways. Some swifts build nests using sticky saliva. Certain snakes use venomous saliva to hunt, injecting it through fangs. Some caterpillars make silk from modified salivary glands.

Larkana district is in the Sindh province of Pakistan. The main city is Larkana. Two former Pakistani prime ministers, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto and Benazir Bhutto, come from this district. Another former leader, Mumtaz Ali Bhutto, was also born here. Actress Sohai Ali Abro and folk singer Abida Parveen are also from Larkana. The Larkana Bulls cricket team was started in 2013. Other towns in the area include Ratodero, Dokri, Bakrani, and Naodero. In 2005, under Prime Minister Pervez Musharraf, the district was split to form a new district called Qamber and Shahdadkot. This new district includes the towns of Qamber Khan and Shahdadkot.

The Eurocopter EC120 Colibri, now called Airbus Helicopters, is a small helicopter that can carry five people. It has one engine and is used for light duties. This helicopter was designed by Eurocopter, CATIC, HAIG, and STAERO in France. In China, the aircraft is made by Hamc as the HC120. They started making it locally in 2004 at their factory in Harbin, a city in northern China. Both the Chinese military and local police have bought these helicopters for use in China.

Madeleine Vionnet, born on June 22, 1876, in Loiret, France, died on March 2, 1975. She was a French fashion designer. Vionnet trained in London before returning to Paris in 1912 to open her first fashion house. It had to close during World War I but reopened after the war. Between 1919 and 1939, she became one of Paris's top designers. In 1939, her house closed again due to World War II, and Vionnet retired in 1940. Known as the "queen of the bias cut" and "the architect among dressmakers," Vionnet is famous for her elegant Grecian-style dresses and for popularizing the bias cut in fashion. Her work inspired many modern designers.
Kuthwal is one of the 51 union councils in Abbottabad district. This district is in Khyber-Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan. It is situated northwest of Abbottabad city, which is the district capital.

Sir Joshua Reynolds was born on July 17, 1723, and died on February 23, 1792. He was an English painter who mainly painted portraits. John Russell said he was one of the most important painters in Europe during the 18th century. Reynolds believed in making paintings that looked perfect even though they weren't real life. In 1769, King George III made him a knight. Reynolds also helped found and became the first president of the Royal Academy of Arts.

Gillingham Football Club is a professional soccer team from Gillingham, Kent, England. The "Gills" play at Priestfield Stadium. They are the only Kent-based team in the Football League and compete in League One, which is the third level of English football. Founded in 1893, they joined the league in 1920. In 1937–38, they were replaced by Ipswich Town but came back to the league 12 years later when it expanded from 88 to 92 teams. Twice in the late 1980s, they nearly won promotion to the second tier but then declined and narrowly avoided relegation to the Football Conference in 1993. From 2000 to 2005, Gillingham were in the second tier for the first time in their history, finishing eleventh in 2002–03.

Daniel Hudson Burnham was an American architect and urban designer, born on September 4, 1846, and died on June 1, 1912. He supported the "Beaux-Arts" movement. Some say he might have been the most successful leader in American architecture. Burnham was a well-known architect in Chicago. In 1892-93, he worked as director of works for the World's Columbian Exposition, often called "The White City." He played important roles in planning cities like Chicago, Manila, Baguio, and Washington D.C.'s downtown area. He also designed famous buildings such as skyscrapers in Chicago, New York City’s Flatiron Building, Union Station in Washington D.C., London's Selfridges department store, and San Francisco’s Merchants Exchange. While he is best known for his skyscrapers and city planning, about a third of Burnham's total work—14.7 million square feet (1.37 million square meters)—was dedicated to shopping buildings.
Vezot is a commune in Sarthe, which is in the Pays de la Loire region. It is located in western France.
Bizen's original center was in the city of Okayama now. From a very early time, Bizen became important for making swords in Japan.

Yandobinskoye is a small village in Russia's Chuvash Republic. It's part of Alikovsky District and located in the central area. The main administrative center nearby is called Yandoba. The population of Yandobinskoye was about 1,081 people as of 2006. This settlement includes twelve smaller rural areas. There is a road that goes through this village.

Jabalpur, known as Jubbulpore until 2006, is a major city in Madhya Pradesh, India. It's called Jabalpur officially now. In 2011, it was the third-largest urban area in Madhya Pradesh and the country’s 38th largest. Famous for Dhuandhar Falls and White Marble Rocks at Bhedaghat, some think snooker began here. Jabalpur is a big administrative, industrial, and business center in Madhya Pradesh. It's an important education place too. The state's high court and many government offices are there. With four main factories making weapons, it’s the city’s top job provider. Other smaller businesses exist. A major trade hub for forest products, Jabalpur grows quickly. As the biggest district in Madhya Pradesh, it has a division named after it. Historically, part of Kalachuri and Rajgond rule, it mixed cultures due to Mughals and Marathas later. In 1800s, British renamed it Jubbulpore. Since India's independence, there are calls for a new state called Mahakoshal with Jabalpur as its capital. The city hosts railway offices, power board, forestry research institute, and army headquarters for five states including Madhya Pradesh. Jabalpur is also home to the Grenadiers and Jammu and Kashmir Rifles army units, along with Signal Training Centre HQ.

In chemistry, an ester is a compound from an acid—organic or inorganic—where at least one hydroxyl group (-OH) is replaced by an alkoxy group. Esters are often made when a carboxylic acid reacts with an alcohol. Fatty acid esters of glycerol, called glycerides, are crucial in biology as major lipids. They form most animal fats and vegetable oils. Esters with small molecular weight are frequently used as fragrances found in essential oils and pheromones. Phosphoesters build DNA molecules. Nitrate esters, like nitroglycerin, are known for their explosive nature. Polyesters, important plastics, consist of monomers bonded by ester groups. Esters typically have a sweet smell and work well as solvents for many plastics, plasticizers, resins, and lacquers. They are also widely used in synthetic lubricants.

Irrigation involves providing water to plants at the right times. It helps grow crops, keep landscapes looking good, and plant new areas when there's not much rain. Irrigation can also protect against frost, stop weeds from growing, and prevent soil from becoming too dense. In contrast, farming that depends only on rain is called rain-fed. Irrigation systems are used for more than just watering plants; they help cool animals, reduce dust, get rid of sewage, and assist in mining. Irrigation is often studied with drainage, which removes extra water from land. People have been using irrigation for over 5,000 years in different cultures around the world, including Asia and parts of America.

Parma is a city in northern Italy, in the Emilia-Romagna region. It's famous for its buildings, music, art, ham called prosciutto, cheese, and beautiful countryside. Parma has an old university, one of the oldest in the world. The city is split by a stream. The area on one side of the river is known as "oltretorrente". In ancient times, when the city was called Parma by the Etruscans, Romans used this name for their round shield. An Italian poet named Attilio Bertolucci, who came from a small village near Parma, wrote: "As a capital, it needed a river. As a smaller capital, it got a stream that is often dry."

A bottle cap or top seals a bottle's opening. It is usually brightly colored and has the brand logo. Plastic caps go on plastic bottles, while glass ones have metal with plastic backing; the metal part is usually steel. Some plastic caps have a pour spout. Flip-top caps provide controlled dispensing of dry products. Different types of plastic are often used for caps compared to bottles.

Kimble County is in Texas, United States. It is on the Edwards Plateau. In 2010, there were 4,607 people living there. The county seat is Junction. Kimble County was formed in 1858 and officially set up in 1876. It is named after George C. Kimble who died at the Battle of the Alamo.

The Salt Fork of the Arkansas River is a small river that joins the Arkansas River. It flows through southern Kansas and northern Oklahoma in the United States. Through the Arkansas River, it becomes part of the Mississippi River's larger water system.

John Elliot, born on May 6, 1898, and died on September 18, 1988, was a British railway manager. His birth name was John Elliot Blumenfeld. He was the son of R.D. Blumenfeld, who worked as the editor for the "Daily Mail." Later, R.D. became managing editor at the "Daily Express." In March 1923, John changed his last name to Elliot—his mother's surname—following advice from Lord Beaverbrook.
Tagusdorf is a commune in Haut-Rhin, which is in Alsace, in northeastern France.
In seismology, the epicenter is the spot on the ground directly above where an earthquake starts. This starting point is called the hypocenter or focus.

Elephant polo is played while riding elephants. It is popular in Nepal, Rajasthan (India), and Thailand. England and Scotland also have teams. Players use a standard ball and sticks made of bamboo. The field is smaller because the elephants move slower. Two people ride each elephant. One person directs the mahout, who steers the elephant. The player tells the mahout where to go and hits the ball. Elephant polo started in Meghauli, Nepal. Tiger Tops in Nepal organizes the game and hosts world championships. In Nepal and Thailand, rules are set by the World Elephant Polo Association (WEPA) to protect elephants. In India and Sri Lanka, events are run separately. An annual tournament was held in Galle, Sri Lanka, under a local association. In 2007, an elephant attacked during a game, hurting players and damaging equipment. Critics said the treatment of polo elephants was cruel. This led to games being canceled and sponsorship ending. Elephant polo records were removed from Guinness World Records. Thailand will stop hosting polo matches in October 2018. An annual tournament at Anantara Hotel Bangkok used to happen there, owned by Minor Hotels.

Eldorado is a city in Saline County, Illinois, United States. Its population was 4,122 at the 2010 census, peaking at 5,198 in 1980. The name "Eldorado" doesn't mean what it sounds like—it originally had a different spelling and meaning. It comes from the last names of two founders: Judge Samuel Elder and his son William, grandson Francis Marion, and neighbor Joseph Reed. Some sources say it was also spelled "elder-redo." According to legend, a signpainter for the railroad changed the name to "Eldorado" on the train depot in 1980. This new spelling has been used ever since, pronounced as "el-do-ray-doh." Eldorado is part of the Illinois-Indiana-Kentucky area and is a suburb within the Harrisburg micropolitan statistical area.
