Murray was an electoral division in Victoria, Australia. It was in the north of the state near the Murray River, which is the border between Victoria and New South Wales. The town areas included were Shepparton, Echuca, Cobram, Yarrawonga, Boort, and Bridgewater. In 2018, it was renamed Nicholls for use at the 2019 federal election.

Greifswald (also called the University and Hanseatic City of Greifswald in German) is a city in northeastern Germany. It's about equally far from Berlin and Hamburg, Germany’s two largest cities, and is around 80 km (50 miles) from the Polish border. Located in Western Pomerania, Greifswald borders the Baltic Sea and has a small river called Ryck running through it. It is near Germany’s two biggest islands, Rügen and Usedom, and close to three of Germany's national parks. Greifswald became the capital of the new district of Vorpommern-Greifswald after changes in September 2011. Together with Stralsund, Greifswald is one of four main cities in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. As of 2013, its population was about 55,659, including many students and workers at the University of Greifswald. Greifswald attracts international interest because of the university, its biocon valley area, the Nord Stream gas pipeline, and the Wendelstein 7-x nuclear fusion project.

Kraftwerk, which means "power station" in German, is a group formed by Ralf Hütter and Florian Schneider in Düsseldorf in 1970. They are known for creating new sounds and being early pioneers of electronic music. Kraftwerk started in West Germany's experimental music scene in the early 1970s and later used lots of machines like synthesizers, drum machines, and vocoders to make their music. They made popular albums such as "Autobahn" (1974), "Trans-Europe Express" (1977), "The Man-Machine" (1978), and "Computer World" (1981). Their music had a special style they called "robot pop," which mixed electronic sounds with catchy tunes, simple arrangements, and repeated beats. They also wore matching suits. Wolfgang Flür left the group in 1987, followed by Karl Bartos in 1990. Florian Schneider left in 2008. Kraftwerk's music has influenced many artists and genres, including synth-pop, hip hop, post-punk, techno, ambient, and club music. In 2014, they received a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award. They won another Grammy for best dance/electronic album with their live album "3-D The Catalogue" in 2018. As of 2020, the band continues to perform.
An anticyclonic storm has wind blowing clockwise around it. This is opposite to the winds around a low-pressure area.
Saint- Jean-sur-Veyle is a town in Ain, which is in eastern France.

Zalmoxes is an extinct genus of dinosaur called a rhabdodontid ornithopod. It lived in Romania during the Maastrichtian period. In 1899, Franz Nopcsa named it as "Mochlodon robustum." Later, in 1915, he reclassified it as "Rhabdodon robustum." In 1990, George Olshevsky changed the name to "Rhabdodon robustus." In 2003, Zalmoxes became the type species when a new species, named Zalmoxes shqiperorum, was identified. This second species was named after Albania, as "shqiperorum" means Albanian in their language. The name "Zalmoxes" comes from the Dacian god Zalmoxis, and "robustus" refers to its strong remains.

Shah Azizur Rahman (23 November 1925 – 1 September 1989) was a politician from Bangladesh. He served as prime minister. However, he faced a lot of controversy for working with Pakistan's army during the fight to create Bangladesh.

Tom Pevsner (born October 2, 1926, and died August 18, 2014) was a British film assistant director and producer. He worked for over four decades. Tom was the second child of Sir Nikolaus Pevsner, an architectural historian from Russia who had Jewish origins. The family moved to Britain in 1933 to escape Nazi Germany. After serving in the British Army from 1944 to 1948, Tom studied languages at Cambridge University. There, he was part of the St John's College Film Society and edited "The Cambridge Review." After graduating, he worked for the Film Finance Corporation. Tom helped make several famous films. He was an assistant director on "The Ladykillers" (1955), "The Longest Day" (1962), and "The Private Life of Sherlock Holmes" (1970). He also produced "Dracula." From the film "For Your Eyes Only" to "Goldeneye," Tom worked as an associate or executive producer for all James Bond films. His work is remembered in "Spectre" when Q mentions a hotel called Pevsner. Tom died at 87 and was honored with a tribute during the 2015 Academy Awards.
Ambleny is a commune located in the Aisne department, which is part of Hauts-de-France in northern France. The people who live there are called Amblenois or Amblenoises.

Myrtle "Kay" Thompson Cagle lived from June 3, 1925, to December 22, 2019. She was an American pilot. Kay Cagle was part of the Mercury 13 group of female astronauts. She worked as a flight instructor and wrote about aviation in North Carolina.

Daniel Michael Devito Jr., born on November 17, 1944, is an American actor. He was famous for playing the taxi dispatcher Louie De Palma in the TV show "Taxi" from 1978 to 1983. This role earned him a Golden Globe and an Emmy award. In another popular show, he plays Frank Reynolds on "It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia," which is still going on since 2006. Devito appeared in many movies such as "One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest" (1975), "Terms of Endearment" (1983), and "Throw Momma from the Train" (1987). He was also in films like "Batman Returns" (1992), "Get Shorty" (1995), and "Matilda" (1996) with his wife Rhea Perlman. Devito is known for his voice roles in movies too, such as "Space Jam" (1996), "Hercules" (1997), and "The Lorax" (2012). He co-founded Jersey Films with Michael Shamberg, and Stacey Sher became a partner later. This company produced films like "Pulp Fiction," "Garden State," and "Freedom Writers." Devito also owned Jersey Television, which made the TV show "Reno 911!". Devito starred in and produced movies together with his wife Rhea Perlman, most notably "Matilda" (1996), based on a Roald Dahl book. He was nominated for an Academy Award as a producer for "Erin Brockovich." Devito has short stature because of a rare genetic condition called multiple epiphyseal dysplasia, or Fairbank's disease.

Healesville Sanctuary is a zoo in rural Victoria, Australia. It was formerly called Sir Colin Mackenzie Sanctuary. The sanctuary focuses on native Australian animals. It has bred many native animals successfully and is one of only two places where platypuses have been born. The other place is Sydney's Taronga Zoo. The sanctuary also helps with breeding endangered Helmeted Honeyeaters. Visitors can see wallabies, wombats, dingoes, kangaroos, and over 200 types of native birds in a natural bushland setting. Paths wind through different habitats. Guided tours, bird shows, and information areas are available for visitors.

Maynard Elliott Solomon, born on January 5, 1930, co-founded Vanguard Records. He was also a music producer. Later, he wrote about famous classical composers from Vienna. He wrote an influential book about Beethoven and essays that won awards. He also wrote a biography about Mozart. In his work about Schubert, Solomon was the first to suggest openly that Schubert might have been gay, even though this idea is not widely accepted.

Potsdam is the largest city in Brandenburg, Germany. It's near Berlin and part of the Berlin/Brandenburg area. Located southwest of Berlin's center, Potsdam was a home for Prussian kings and German emperors until 1918. Its design shows ideas from the Enlightenment era. It has nice parks and palaces, especially Sanssouci, which is a big UNESCO site in Germany. The Potsdam Conference happened at Cecilienhof palace in 1945. In the southeast of Potsdam, Babelsberg was a major film studio since the 1930s. It became important for making films after the Berlin Wall fell. Today, it's still one of Europe’s key film production centers and is called Filmstudio Babelsberg. Potsdam also became an important science center in the 1800s. Now, there are three colleges, the University of Potsdam, and over 30 research places in the city.

Michael Gregory Rowe was born on March 18, 1962. He is from the United States and has worked as a TV host, narrator, and used to sing in an opera. He is famous for being on the Discovery Channel show "Dirty Jobs" and another series called "Somebody's Got To Do It," which was first made for CNN. Now he hosts a Facebook series named "Returning the Favor." In this, he finds people doing good things and does something nice for them in return. He also has his own podcast called "The Way I Heard It with Mike Rowe." This podcast tells short stories meant for curious minds that have trouble focusing. Michael has narrated shows on different channels like Discovery Channel, Science Channel, and National Geographic, such as "Deadliest Catch," "How the Universe Works," and "Shark Week." He has also appeared in ads for companies like Ford Motor Company. In June 2020, the Discovery Channel said they would show four episodes of "Dirty Jobs: Rowe'd Trip" in mid-July 2020. These episodes were called a mix of a reunion, a road trip, and a look-back special.

Hedemora is a town in Dalarna County, Sweden. In 2010, it had about 7, 273 people living there. Although small, Hedemora is called a "city" because of its history. It is the oldest city in the county. Some people from Hedemora include Jonas Nilsson and Kerstin Thorborg. Others are Martin Matsbo, Bertil Norman, and Ulf Stenlund. Hedemora makes diesel engines for ships. These engines can be found in submarines built by Kockums, like those used by the Royal Australian Navy and the Republic of Singapore Navy. Clifftop Games is based in Hedemora. They make video games, such as Kathy Rain and Whispers of a Machine.
Septèmes-les-Vallons is a small town in southern France, in an area called Bouches-du-Rhône. It is about 10. 7 kilometers or 6. 5 miles north of Marseille's center.

Questacon, the national science and tech center, is on Lake Burley Griffin in Canberra, Australia. It has over 200 hands-on exhibits about science and tech. Questacon also offers many programs to encourage Australian kids to enjoy science.

Edgar Lawrence Doctorow, born on January 6, 1931, and passed away on July 21, 2015, was an American writer. He is famous for his historical fiction novels. He wrote twelve novels and three volumes of short stories, as well as a stage play. Some of his most awarded books are "Ragtime" (1975), "Billy Bathgate" (1989), and "The March" (2005). These works often placed fictional characters in real historical events alongside known figures. His stories were praised for their creativity, and he was recognized for his bold imagination. Many of Doctorow's novels and short stories were adapted into films and plays. Notable adaptations include "Welcome to Hard Times" with Henry Fonda (1967), "Daniel" with Timothy Hutton (1983), "Billy Bathgate" with Dustin Hoffman (1991), and "Wakefield" with Bryan Cranston (2016). His work was most famous for the film version of "Ragtime" (1981) and its stage adaptation, which won four Tony Awards. Doctorow received several awards, including the National Book Critics Circle Award for "Ragtime," "Billy Bathgate," and "The March," as well as the American Academy of Arts and Letters Gold Medal for Fiction. Former President Barack Obama called him one of America's greatest novelists.
Launay-Villiers is a commune located in the Mayenne department. This area is in western France.

James Albert Smith Leach was born on October 15, 1942. He is an American who used to work as a teacher and politician. From 2009 to 2013, he was the ninth chair of the National Endowment for the Humanities. Before that, from 1977 to 2007, he worked in the U.S. House of Representatives for Iowa. Leach had a long career as a Republican member of Congress for 30 years. He represented Iowa's 1st district until 2003. In Congress, Leach led the House Committee on Banking and Financial Services from 1995 to 2001. He was also in charge of a subcommittee dealing with Asian and Pacific affairs from 2001 to 2006. He helped create and co-chaired the Congressional Humanities Caucus. In 2006, he lost his election to Dave Loebsack, who belonged to another political party. Notably, Leach supported a significant banking law called the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act in 1999.
Karl-Josef Rauber was born on April 11, 1934. He is a cardinal in the Catholic Church. From 1982 to 2009, he worked as a papal nuncio.

Suseok, also called viewing stones or scholar's rocks, is a Korean term for naturally occurring or shaped small rocks traditionally valued. These stones are similar to Chinese gongshi and Japanese suiseki. Suseok can be any color. They come in various sizes—ranging from less than one kilogram to hundreds of kilograms. This term also includes the rocks placed in traditional Korean gardens.

Glynis Johns, born on October 5, 1923, is a retired actress, dancer, pianist, and singer from Britain. She was born in Pretoria, South Africa, while her parents were performing there. Glynis is famous for creating the role of Desiree Armfeldt in "A Little Night Music" on Broadway. For this role, she won a Tony Award. She also played Winifred Banks in Walt Disney's musical movie "Mary Poppins." In these roles, she sang special songs written just for her, such as "Send in the Clowns," by Stephen Sondheim, and "Sister Suffragette," by The Sherman Brothers. Glynis was nominated for an Oscar for her acting in the 1960 film "The Sundowners." Her voice has a distinctive, deep quality, and she is known for being cheerful on stage.
Manuele Blasi was born on August 17, 1980. He was an Italian soccer player who played as a midfielder.

Ketchikan is a city and the main town in the Ketchikan Gateway Borough, Alaska. It's the state's southeasternmost large community. Downtown Ketchikan is recognized as a national historic district. As of 2010, it had about 8,050 people, making it the fifth-largest city and the tenth-biggest place when smaller areas are counted too. The surrounding area, including nearby towns north and south along the Tongass Highway (most considered part of Ketchikan), plus small rural settlements accessible by water, had around 13,477 in the same year. By 2017, it was estimated to have about 13,754 people. Ketchikan became an officially incorporated city on August 25, 1900, which is earlier than any other city in Alaska due to changes in other areas. The city sits on Revillagigedo Island, named by Captain George Vancouver in 1793. Ketchikan got its name from a creek that runs through the town and empties into the Tongass Narrows. "Ketchikan" comes from Tlingit language but its exact meaning is not clear—it could mean "the river belonging to kitschk" or "thundering wings of an eagle."

Jealousy means feeling worried or afraid because you think someone has something better than you. These feelings can also include anger, disappointment, or a sense that things aren't fair. The word "jealousy" used to mean different things from "envy," but now they are often the same. People feel jealous in their relationships, and even very young babies show signs of jealousy as early as five months old. Some experts say everyone feels jealous, while others think it depends on culture. Jealousy can be about doubting someone or reacting to what you see. It usually involves a mix of strong feelings. Scientists have looked at why people feel jealous and found some reasons for it. Sociologists have shown that the beliefs and values in your culture affect when and how people show jealousy. Biologists have also noticed unconscious factors influencing jealousy. Artists from different times and places have explored jealousy in their works, like paintings, songs, and books. Religious leaders give their views on jealousy based on their religious teachings.

Red is at the end of what we see when light shows, next to orange. It's opposite violet. Red has a main wavelength between about 625 to 740 nanometres. In color models like RGB and CMYK, red is one of the primary colors. The color directly opposite it is cyan. Red comes in many shades, from bright yellowish scarlet and vermillion to bluish crimson. It can be very light pink or dark burgundy. People used red ochre pigment in some of the first artworks made by early humans. In ancient Egypt and Mayan ceremonies, people colored their faces red. Roman generals were often painted red after winning battles. Red was also important in China, where it was used for early pottery and later palace gates and walls. During the Renaissance, nobles wore bright red clothing dyed with kermes and cochineal. The 19th century brought synthetic red dyes that replaced traditional ones. Red became a symbol of revolution; countries like Soviet Russia, China, Vietnam, and others used it on their flags after revolutions in the early 20th century. Red reminds us of blood, so it's linked to sacrifice, danger, and bravery. Surveys show people often connect red with heat, activity, passion, sexuality, anger, love, and joy in Europe and the US. In China, India, and many other Asian countries, red means happiness and good fortune.
Code name: Kids Next Door—Operation S.O.D.A. is a platformer video game from America based on an animated TV show. It came out only for Game Boy Advance in 2004.
cléden-poher is a village in Finistère, which is in Brittany. Brittany is in northwest France.

A combat sport is a competitive sport that involves fighting. Usually, it's between two people. In many of these sports, one contestant wins by getting more points than the other or by making the opponent unable to fight back. Some common combat sports are mixed martial arts, boxing, wrestling, judo, and kickboxing.

The Zitter Forest is found in parts of Germany and Belgium. It covers an area between Hellenthal, Dahlem, Kronenburg, and Büllingen. This forest is part of the Hohes Venn–Eifel nature park. To the north, it borders the Eifel National Park; to the south, the River Kyll forms its southern boundary. The Zitter Forest is mostly on hills between 500 and 692 meters high. Its highest point is at Weissstein (692 meters), which has ski slopes. Other notable hills include Bärbelkreuz (662.8 meters), Hühnerhöhe (659.9 meters), and Kamberg (637.8 meters). Several villages like Giescheid, Miescheid, Neuhaus, Ramscheid, and Udenbreth are in the northern part of Zitter Forest. These areas are some of the highest parishes in Rhineland. The Zitter Forest is home to wildcats. There’s also a transmission tower called Eifel-Bärbelkreuz within it.

Islamgarh was formerly called Akalgarh. It is in Mirpur district near the Mangla Dam in Azad Jammu and Kashmir. Located south of the Pir Panjal mountain range, Islamgarh is about 28 kilometers northeast of Mirpur. In 2017, it had a population of 16,651 people.

Mallika Sherawat, born on October 24, 1976, is a well-known Indian actress who mainly works in Hindi movies. She became famous for her bold role in films like "Khwahish" and "Murder," where she was seen as a sex symbol. She starred in the romantic comedy "Pyaar Ke Side Effects" (2006) which received good reviews from critics. After this, she appeared in successful movies such as "Aap Ka Suroor" and "Welcome" (both in 2007), her biggest hit so far, and "Double Dhamaal" (2011). She is one of the few Bollywood actors trying to work in Hollywood with films like "Hissss" (2010) and "Politics of Love" (2011).

Grenay is a town in France. It is located in the Pas-de-Calais department, which is part of Hauts-de-France region. Grenay belongs to the Lens arrondissement and Wingles canton. The commune also forms part of the Lens-Liévin urban area. In 2013, Grenay had 6,899 people living there. The mayor resigned on March 31, 2019, and was replaced by his deputy Mathieu Feutry until an election could be held.
As of October 1, 2016, the city had about 65,075 people living there. That means there were roughly 7,300 people for every square kilometer. The city covers an area of around 8.9 square kilometers.
Distribution can mean: spreading something out delivering items to different places

Ricardo Montaner is an Argentine-Venezuelan singer and songwriter. His first album, named after him, came out in 1986. The album was released by Sono-Rodven Discos. It topped the Billboard Latin Pop Albums chart.
L-upsingen is a municipality in the district of Liestal, which is in the canton of Basel-Country in Switzerland.

Saydabad district is in Maidan Wardak province in Afghanistan. It has a pleasant climate with hills, streams, and orchards. Saydabad was a popular place for people from Kabul to visit until fighting increased in 2000s. The city of Saydabad is the capital of this district. It has more than 114,793 people living there, making it the biggest district in the province. Saydabad is in an area mainly inhabited by Pashtuns.

Lewis Collins was born on May 27, 1946, and died on November 27, 2013. He was an actor in films and theatre. His most famous role was playing 'Bodie' in a British TV show called "The Professionals" from the late 1970s to early 1980s.

Christian Karembeu, born on December 3, 1970, was a French footballer. He is now an advisor for Olympiacos. During his career as a player, he played for several teams including Nantes, Sampdoria, Real Madrid, Middlesbrough, Olympiacos, Servette, and Bastia. Karembeu also played for the French national team, which won the 1998 FIFA World Cup in France. He participated in one match during France's UEFA Euro 2000 championship. Born in New Caledonia, a French overseas territory, Karembeu is part of a group based in Paris that plans to add a Pacific island team to the A-League.

A community is a group of people who have things in common, like rules, beliefs, or customs. They might live in the same place or connect through communication. Strong bonds exist beyond just family connections. These bonds are important for roles in groups like families, jobs, governments, and societies. Communities can be small, like a neighborhood, or large, like a country or online group. The word "community" comes from Latin, meaning shared things and common spirit. People in a community often share goals, beliefs, resources, preferences, and concerns. This helps define who they are and how closely they work together.

Chess Records was an American record company, started by two Jewish brothers named Leonard and Phil Chess from Poland. They founded it in Chicago in 1950. At first, they focused on blues music but later added rhythm and blues, soul, gospel, early rock and roll, jazz, and comedy recordings. They released their music under the Chess label and some smaller labels like Checker, Argo/Cadet, and Cadet Concept. Today, Universal Music Group owns all of Chess Records' music, managed by Geffen Records. Chess produced many important songs that are part of rock music history. Critic Cub Koda said Chess was "America's greatest blues label." The company had offices in different places on Chicago’s south side. Their most famous location was 2120 S. Michigan Avenue from May 1957 to 1965. The Rolling Stones recorded there during their first U.S. tour in 1964 and again later. They called this place Chess Studios, though it officially was Ter-Mar studios. Chess moved to a bigger building at 320 E. 21st Street in the mid-1960s, which used to be Revere Camera Company. Leonard Chess died in 1969, and before he passed away, he sold the company to his brother Phil.

typesetting involves arranging letters and symbols to make text. In older methods, these are physical pieces called sorts; in digital systems, they are called glyphs. The arrangement follows the rules of writing for a particular language. Typesetting uses fonts, which some mistakenly think are the same as typefaces. An important result was that it became easier to identify who wrote something, making unauthorized copying harder.

Karch Kiraly, born on November 3, 1960, is from America. He played volleyball, coached, and did broadcasts. In the 1980s, he was part of the U.S. national volleyball team that won gold medals in 1984 and 1988 Olympic Games. He also won another gold medal at the 1996 Olympics. This was the first time beach volleyball was in the Olympics. Kiraly is unique as he's the only person, male or female, to win Olympic gold in both indoor and beach volleyball. He played college volleyball for UCLA. His teams there won three national championships under coach Al Scates. Now, Karch Kiraly leads the U.S. women’s national volleyball team.

The glass frogs belong to a group of frogs called centrolenidae, which is part of the amphibian family. Most of these frogs have a green color. However, some can be seen with their insides, like their heart and stomach, through their skin on their bellies. That's why they are called glass frogs. Glass frogs live mainly in trees. They come down for mating only during specific times.

Paul Anthony Samuelson was an American economist, born on May 15, 1915, and died on December 13, 2009. He became the first American to win the Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences in 1970. The Swedish Royal Academy said he raised economic theory to a higher scientific level more than any other economist of his time. Samuelson was considered one of the top economists of the 20th century, and President Bill Clinton praised him for over six decades of important contributions to economics when Samuelson received the National Medal of Science in 1996. He believed that math was essential for economists and wrote a book called "Foundations of Economic Analysis" which helped make economic theory more mathematical. His most famous work is "Economics: An Introductory Analysis," the best-selling economics textbook ever, first published in 1948. It has been updated many times, selling millions of copies in different languages. James Poterba, who used to lead MIT’s economics department, said Samuelson left a big legacy as both a researcher and teacher. Samuelson started college at the University of Chicago when he was just 16 years old during the Great Depression. He earned his PhD from Harvard University. At age 25, he became an assistant professor at MIT and rose to full professor by 32. In 1966, he received MIT's highest honor, the Institute Professor award. Throughout his career, Samuelson attracted other famous economists like Robert Solow, Franco Modigliani, Robert Merton, Joseph Stiglitz, and Paul Krugman to join MIT’s faculty. Many of them later won Nobel Prizes. He advised Presidents John F. Kennedy and Lyndon B. Johnson, and worked as a consultant for the U.S. Treasury, the Bureau of the Budget, and the President's Council of Economic Advisers. Samuelson wrote weekly columns in Newsweek magazine with Milton Friedman from the Chicago School of economics, representing opposing views on economic theories. Their 1967 columns earned Newsweek a special award.

richard benaud, born on october 6, 1930, and who passed away on april 10, 2015, was an australian cricketer. After he stopped playing international cricket in 1964, he became known for his cricket commentary. Benaud played as both a bowler and a batsman at the test level. He combined leg spin bowling with aggressive lower-order batting. Together with another all-rounder named alan davidson, they helped make australia the best team in world cricket during the late 1950s and early 1960s after a period of poor performance in the early 1950s. In 1958, he became the captain of the test team. He retired from playing in 1964. He was the first cricketer to reach both 200 wickets and 2,000 runs in test cricket by 1963. gideon haigh thought benaud might be "the most influential cricketer and personality since world war ii." according to harold de andrado from sri lanka, richard benaud was one of the greatest figures in cricket as a player, researcher, writer, critic, author, organizer, adviser, and student of the game.

Gliese 667 CC, also called GJ 667CC, HR 6426CC, or HD 156384CC, is an exoplanet. It orbits a red dwarf star named Gliese 667 C. Gliese 667 C is part of a triple star system. The exoplanet is in the habitable zone of its star. It is about 23. 62 light-years away, or roughly 217 billion kilometers, in the Scorpius constellation. Scientists found this exoplanet by looking at how the star's spectrum showed changes due to the planet's gravitational pull.

Hemphill is a city in Sabine County, Texas, United States. It had 1,198 people in the 2010 census. Hemphill is the county seat of Sabine County. The city is on State Highway 87 where it meets State Highway 184. Hemphill is surrounded by the Sabine National Forest and Toledo Bend Reservoir.

Carla Bozulich, born on December 24, 1965, is an American musician based in Los Angeles. She is known as the lead singer, lyricist, and founder of the Geraldine Fibbers and Evangelista. She was also a founding member of Ethyl Meatplow and Scarnella. The Geraldine Fibbers made two albums for Virgin Records. Their first album, "Lost Somewhere Between the Earth and My Home," was called "a country feedback masterpiece" by Vice. In 2006, Bozulich started her project Evangelista with an album named after herself. The album was released by Constellation Records in Montreal, Quebec. In 2007, The Sunday Times said about the album: "Evangelista is a vivid inner darkness that outshines rock's weeping millionaires." From 2008 to 2011, Bozulich used Evangelista as a project name for albums "Hello, Voyager," "Prince of Truth," and "In Animal Tongue." Her consistent band members include bassist Tara Barnes, keyboardist Dominic Cramp, guitarist Nels Cline, violinist Jessica Moss, organist Nadia Moss, drummer Ches Smith, and multi-instrumentalist co-producer. Various musicians from Godspeed! You Black Emperor helped arrange, record, and write songs with Evangelista. The band lineup changes for each performance or recording session. The "Hello, Voyager" album includes 14 different musicians on different tracks. In 2014, Constellation released an album under Bozulich's name as a solo artist called "Boy." Her latest album, "Quieter," was released in May 2018 and is a collection of previously unreleased songs. Bozulich has also worked with Francesco Guerri, Novariant/Sarah Lipstate, and Devin Sarno on other projects.
Arkelstorp is a place located in Kristianstad Municipality, Skåne County, Sweden. In December 2010, there were 768 people living there.

A leaf blower, known as a blower, moves leaves and grass. It uses air from an electric or gasoline engine to clear debris. Gasoline models often had two-stroke engines but now have four-stroke ones too. Four-stroke engines help reduce air pollution. Leaf blowers are usually small, handheld tools. Some are backpack-mounted with a wand for better handling during long use. Larger units on wheels can also be pushed like a cart. There are bigger leaf blowers called "walk behind" models that need to be pushed manually. Some can suck up leaves and small branches into a bag as they clean, acting like a vacuum cleaner. This type is often called a blower vac.

Sheyi Emmanuel Adeyobor, born on February 26, 1984, is a Togolese football player who plays as a striker. He has played for several clubs, including Arsenal and Manchester City in England, Monaco in France, Real Madrid in Spain, Istanbul Başakşehir and Kayserispor in Turkey, and Olimpia Asunción in Paraguay. In 2008, while at Arsenal, he was named African Footballer of the Year. His most significant moment came when he joined Olimpia Asunción in 2020; he became a very famous player in Paraguayan football and the highest-paid player in the country's history. Adeyobor played for Togo in the 2006 FIFA World Cup, which was the first time Togo participated. He stopped playing for the national team after an incident where their bus was shot at during a trip to Angola for the 2010 Africa Cup of Nations. However, he returned to play for Togo in the 2013 Africa Cup of Nations and helped them reach the quarter-finals. As of now, Adeyobor is Togo's all-time top goalscorer with 32 goals.

Andrzej Wojciech Suski, born on December 24, 1941, is a retired Polish Catholic priest. He was born in Płock. Suski became a priest in 1965. From 1986 to 1992, he worked as an auxiliary bishop of Płock. In 1992, he became the bishop of Toruń. He retired in November 2017.
Bodcaw is a town in Arkansas, United States. It is in Nevada County. In 2000, there were 154 people living there. Bodcaw is part of the Hope micropolitan statistical area.

An observation deck is an elevated area where you can look at views. It's often found on tall buildings like skyscrapers or observation towers. Sometimes, these decks are sheltered from the weather. Some observation decks even have telescopes you can use with coins to see distant sights.
William Thomas Hart was born on February 4, 1929. He is an older judge who works in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois.

Sportverein Grödig is an Austrian soccer club from Grödig. The team plays in the Austrian Regional League West, which is the third level of Austrian football. At the end of the 2015–16 season, Grödig were promoted out of the Austrian Bundesliga. However, due to financial problems, they moved down two levels and are now in the Austrian Regional League West.

Donnan Allan Pennebaker, often known as D.A. Pennebaker, was an American documentary filmmaker who lived from July 15, 1925, to August 1, 2019. He made films about performing arts and politics and is considered one of the pioneers of direct cinema. In 2013, he received an Academy Honorary Award for his work. People have called him "likely the most important documenter of 1960s counterculture."

Jiang Yi-huai was born on November 18, 1960. He is a Taiwanese politician. Jiang used to be the premier of the Republic of China (ROC). On November 29, 2014, he resigned and was replaced by Mao Chi-kuo on December 8, 2014. Before becoming premier, Jiang was vice premier from 2012 to 2013. He also held other positions: minister of the interior from 2009 to 2012, and minister of research, development, and evaluation commission of the executive yuan from 2008 to 2009.

Voltage, which is also called electric potential difference, electric pressure, or electric tension, measures the difference in electric potential between two points. In a static electric field, it's the work needed to move a test charge from one point to another. The SI unit for voltage (potential difference) is volt. Work done per unit of charge is measured in volts; 1 volt equals 1 joule of work per coulomb of charge. Since 1990, volt was defined using the quantum Hall and Josephson effects. In 2019, fundamental physical constants were used to define all SI units and derived units, including voltage. Voltage or electric potential difference is often denoted by V or U in symbols. A voltmeter can measure this difference between two points. Voltage can be caused by charge, current through a magnetic field, time-varying fields, or combinations of these. Voltage represents energy from sources (electromotive force) or energy used or stored.

Lars Mortimer was born on March 22, 1946. He was a comic artist from Sweden who drew and wrote stories for comic strips like "Bubo" and "Hälgé." Lars passed away due to an illness in Alfta, Hälsingland on August 25, 2014. He was 68 years old at the time.

A blast injury happens because of an explosion, whether it is direct or indirect. When there's an explosion from powerful or less strong bombs, people can get hurt. This harm is worse if the explosion takes place in a small area.

Jose C. Vitug, born on July 15, 1934, is a Filipino lawyer and judge. He became an associate justice at the Supreme Court of the Philippines in 1993 when President Fidel Ramos appointed him. Vitug stopped working as a justice in 2004. He also started the Angeles University Foundation School of Law. Currently, he works as a director for Abbotiz Equity Ventures.

The British Rail Class 304 electric trains were made for use in suburban areas on parts of the West Coast Main Line between Crewe and Manchester/Liverpool/Rugby. They started as AM4 but later became Class 304 under a new numbering system. These trains operated mainly on the West Coast Main Line. Based on the 1959 design, they looked similar to Classes 305, 308, and some 1,200-volt DC Class 504 units. None of these trains were saved for museums, and all were eventually recycled.

Sir Herbert Edwardes was born on November 12, 1819, and died on December 23, 1868. He worked as an administrator, soldier, and statesman in British India, especially in the Punjab region. People remember him most for his important role during the Second Anglo-Sikh War, where he helped the British win.

Ambrières-les-Vallées is a village in the Mayenne department, which is in Northwestern France. It is near Normandy.

Jean-Michel Larrasket, born on May 22, 1950, and who passed away on March 19, 2018, was a French professor and engineer. He also served as the vice president of the French Basque country in the Basque Studies Society. He promoted projects to help the social and economic growth of the French Basque country. Additionally, he helped found Éticoop, a cooperative that supports starting businesses in this region.

Ingram Olkin, born on July 23, 1924, and died on April 28, 2016, was a professor at Stanford University. He worked in both the statistics department and the Graduate School of Education. Olkin helped develop ways to study policies, especially those related to education. He also made important contributions to meta-analysis, teaching statistics, studying many variables together, and majorization theory.

Ramo Peter Ceresino was born on April 24, 1929, and died on May 1, 2015. He played ice hockey as a left winger for the Toronto Maple Leafs in the NHL. Ramo married Lorraine Giardetti on June 2, 1953, and they stayed together for 62 years. In 1962, he moved his family to California and lived in Los Angeles, where he worked as a mortgage broker. Later, he retired to San Diego. He had three children, one of them being Gordon Ceresino.

Bartolomeo Alberto Cappellari, who later became Pope Gregory XVI, lived from September 18, 1765, to June 1, 1846. He was the leader of the Catholic Church and ruled over the Papal States from February 2, 1831, until his death. He chose the name Mauro when he joined the Camaldolese religious order. As a strong conservative, Gregory XVI did not like changes in laws or society, especially those that promoted democracy or modern ideas. He thought these were dangerous and could lead to revolution. To strengthen the power of the Pope, he supported missionary work overseas and spoke against slavery. However, his tough rule and spending money on himself made people dislike him a lot at home. Gregory XVI was the last pope to use the name "Gregory." He was also the last person who wasn't a bishop to become Pope, until Pope Francis became Pope in 2013. He was the most recent Pope who had been part of a religious order before becoming Pope.
In economics and political economy, returns are distributions or payments given to people who provide goods or services.

World music is a category of Western music that includes various styles from other parts of the globe. It covers music that people in the West consider ethnic, indigenous, folk, or a mix of non-Western and Western popular music. This type of music doesn't have one clear definition because it's so diverse, but it focuses on interesting sounds from different cultures. The term "world music" became popular in the 1980s for marketing non-Western traditional music. Over time, it has expanded to include subgenres like ethnic fusion and worldbeat.

Mortality rate means how many deaths happen in a group of people every year, for each 1,000 individuals. For example, if there are 9.5 deaths out of 1,000 people in a year, it is called a mortality rate of 9.5 per 1,000. This is different from "morbidity," which is about how many people have a disease, or the number of new cases appearing each year. An important way to look at mortality rates is through crude death rate. It measures all deaths in a population over a certain time period. For instance, the CIA estimates that globally, 7.7 out of every 1,000 people will die each year. To calculate mortality rates, you use this formula: mortality rate = (number of deaths / size of the population) × conversion factor. The conversion factor helps change the fraction into a number per 1,000 individuals, for example.

Rameswaram is a town and municipality located in Tamil Nadu's Ramanathapuram district. It sits on Pamban Island, separated from mainland India by the Pamban Channel. Pamban Island connects to mainland India via the Pamban Bridge. About 40 kilometers away lies Mannar Island in Sri Lanka. Rameswaram is at the southern tip of the Indian peninsula in the Gulf of Mannar. It's an important place for Hindus because it's part of the Char Dham pilgrimage and considered one of the holiest sites in India. According to the Ramayana, Rama built a bridge from here to Lanka with Hanuman’s help to rescue his wife Sita. The town center features the Ramanathaswamy Temple, which is dedicated to Lord Shiva and connected to Rama's story. The temple and the town are considered sacred by Shaivas. Rameswaram is close to Sri Lanka and has been linked to it in geological history as well. It's involved in discussions about projects like the Sethusamudram Shipping Canal, disputes over Kachchatheevu island, and issues related to Tamil refugees from Sri Lanka and local fishermen. Established as a municipality in 1994, Rameswaram covers an area of around. In 2011, it had a population of 44,856. Most people there work in tourism or fishing.

Plains is a town in West Texas, United States. It is located in Yoakum County, specifically in the southern part of the Panhandle Plains region. The town's population was 1,481 according to the 2010 census.

Hiragana and katakana are both writing systems used in Japanese. Each syllable or sound in Japanese is shown with one character or a pair of characters in these systems. Hiragana can be vowels like "a" (written あ), consonants followed by vowels like "ka" (written か), or nasal sounds that can be like English "m," "n," or "ng." These are called syllabic symbols, not letters. Hiragana is used for writing suffixes after kanji, such as to make verbs and adjectives change form. It also writes words without kanji, or when the kanji form is too formal or hard to read. Sometimes writers use hiragana instead of kanji just for a casual feel. Hiragana can also show how to pronounce kanji. There are two ways to order hiragana: the old iroha system and the more common gojūon system.
San Diego is a city in Duval County, Texas, United States. As of the 2010 census, its population was 4,488. The city mainly lies in Duval County and serves as the county seat.

Linux Mint is a Linux computer system that people work on together. It uses Ubuntu or Debian. It includes many free programs. You can also choose to add some special software during installation if you want better multimedia support. The project was started by Clément Lefèbvre and is developed by the Linux Mint team and community.

Our band could be your life: Scenes from the American indie underground, 1981-1991 is a book by Michael Azerrad. He wrote about several rock bands that didn't gain much attention from big music companies but were very important in creating alternative and indie music in America. They achieved this mainly through lots of touring and releasing records on small independent labels. Azerrad talked to many band members and also looked at old fanzines, as well as mainstream newspapers and books for information.

Everland is South Korea's largest theme park. It is in Yongin, a city in Gyeonggi-do. Everland has 5.85 million visitors each year and was the nineteenth most popular amusement park worldwide in 2018. The park includes attractions, a zoo called Caribbean Bay, and a water park. Everland is run by Samsung C&T Corporation, part of the Samsung Group. It used to be known as "Jayeon Nongwon," which means "natural farm." Its old English name was "Farmland."
Warendorf is a district in northern North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It borders districts like Steinfurt, Osnabrück, Gütersloh, Soest, Hamm (a city), Coesfeld, and Münster (another city).

Frank Cloud Cooksey, born on June 3, 1933, is an American public servant. In the 1950s, he was the president of the student body at the University of Texas. He worked as a lawyer in different places. First, he was with the U.S. District Attorney's Civil Rights Division. Then, he worked for John Hill at the Texas Attorney General's Office. After that, he had his own law practice. From 1985 to 1988, he served as the mayor of Austin, Texas. He is also known for being an environmental activist and for having progressive ideas when he was mayor.

José Hugo Garaycoa Hawkins was a Roman Catholic bishop. He was born in Peru on June 2, 1930, and became a priest in 1961. From 1982 to 1991, he worked as the titular bishop of Horaea and an auxiliary bishop in the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Lima, Peru. Later, from 1991 to 2006, he served as the bishop of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Tacna y Moquegua, Peru. He passed away on March 27, 2018.

Achim Mentzel, born in Berlin on July 15, 1946, died in Cottbus on January 4, 2016. He was a German musician, TV host, and actor. His most famous show was "Achims Hitparade," which he hosted from 1989 to 2006. He also worked with Oliver Kalkofe in the show "Kalkofes Mattscheibe." Between 1978 and 2010, Mentzel released 23 singles and seven albums. He was part of a cover band called Fritzens Dampferband, along with Nina Hagen. Mentzel appeared in films like "The Legend of Paul and Paula" (1973) and "Der Wixxer" (2004), as well as TV shows such as "Das Amt" and "Leipzig Homicide." He got married four times and had eight children. The cause of his death was believed to be a heart attack or stroke.

Arsène Lupin is a pretend thief and very good at disguising himself. He was created in 1905 by French writer Maurice Leblanc. The character's name was changed from Arsène Lopin because a local politician with the same name complained. His story, "The Arrest of Arsène Lupin," appeared in July 15, 1905, in a magazine called "Je Sais Tout." Maurice Leblanc wrote 17 novels and 39 shorter stories about Lupin, making a total of 24 books. If we count the 1923 novel "The Secret Tomb," there are 25 books in total. In this book, Dorothée solves one of Arsène Lupin's four famous mysteries without Lupin appearing. Arsène Lupin also appeared in many other stories written by different authors and has been made into films, TV shows, plays, and comics. Five more books about him were written in the 1970s by a mystery writing team named Boileau-Narcejac.

Tuili is a municipality in the province of South Sardinia, in the Italian region of Sardinia. It is located north of Cagliari and northeast of Sanluri. Tuili borders these municipalities: Barumini, Gesturi, Las Plassas, Pauli Arbarei, Setzu, and Turri.

Alain Emile Louis Marie Poher was born on April 17, 1909, and died on December 9, 1996. He was a French politician from the center of the political spectrum. At first, he was with the Popular Republican Movement. Later, he joined the Democratic Centre. Poher worked as a senator for Val-de-Marne from 1946 to 1995. From October 3, 1968, to October 1, 1992, he served as the president of the Senate. During this time, he also acted as the country's interim president twice. Poher was one of the main candidates in the 1969 presidential election but lost to Georges Pompidou in the second round.

Cipriano de Rore (occasionally spelled Cypriano) was born around 1515 or 1516 and died between September 11 and 20, 1565. He was a composer from France or Flanders who worked during the Renaissance period. De Rore was important because he moved to Italy to work and represent a new generation of Franco-Flemish composers after Josquin des Prez. He was also one of the best madrigal composers in the mid-16th century. His music, which used new sounds and expressed strong feelings, greatly influenced later madrigal compositions.

Luis Maldonado Venegas, born November 19, 1956, and passed away on April 30, 2019, was a Mexican politician and lawyer. He worked for the Party of the Democratic Revolution. Maldonado served as a federal deputy representing Mexico City and the fourth electoral region in the 63rd legislature of the Mexican Congress. Additionally, he became the national president of the Convergencia party and represented it in both houses of Congress.

Metamorphic rocks come from changes in existing rocks through a process called metamorphism, which means "change in form." The original rock (protolith) is changed by heat (over 150 to 200°C) and pressure. This can happen below the Earth's surface where other rocks are present. Sedimentary, igneous, or previously formed metamorphic rocks can turn into metamorphic rocks. These rocks make up a large part of the Earth’s crust and cover about 12% of the land surface. They are grouped by their texture and the minerals they contain (metamorphic facies). Metamorphic rocks can form when deep underground heat is applied, or when there's high pressure from layers above. Sometimes, these rocks are created during tectonic movements, like when continents collide. This causes horizontal pressure, friction, and distortion. They can also be formed by heat from hot molten rock (magma) inside the Earth. Studying metamorphic rocks that are now on the surface tells us about deep underground conditions. Examples of these rocks include gneiss, slate, marble, schist, and quartzite.

Alzey-Worms is a district in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. It is next to (following a clockwise direction) the Groß-Gerau district (which is in Hesse), the city of Worms, and districts called Bad Dürkheim, Donnersbergkreis, Bad Kreuznach, and Mainz-Bingen.
maspie-lalnumque-juillacq is a commune in Pyrénées-Atlantiques, which is in southwestern France.
Jan Zweyer was born on December 12, 1953, in Frankfurt (Main). He is a German writer. Jan Zweyer is his pen name; his real name is Rüdiger Richartz.

This list includes South African rivers. Many names have the Afrikaans suffix "-rivier". Sometimes, you'll see "-kamma", which comes from a Khoisan word for "river". Often, English "river" is also added to the name. Zulu uses "amanzi" (meaning water) in some river names. In Afrikaans, small rivers are sometimes called "spruit" (similar to spring).

Siġġiewi, also called Città Ferdinando, is a city and local council in southern Malta. It is the third largest council by area after Rabat and Mellieħa. Situated on a plateau near Mdina, the ancient capital, and Valletta, the current capital, it had 8,367 inhabitants as of March 2014. In the past, most people worked in nearby fields. In 1993, Siġġiewi adopted the motto "work and virtue."

Bhagat Singh Koshyari, born on June 17, 1942, is an Indian politician. He currently serves as the governor of Maharashtra and has additional responsibilities for Goa. As a long-time member of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), he held several important positions in the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). He was the national vice president of BJP and the party's first state president for Uttarakhand. Koshyari also served as the second chief minister of Uttarakhand, now known as Uttaranchal, from 2001 to 2002. After that, he became the leader of the opposition in the Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly from 2002 to 2003. He worked as an MLC (Member of Legislative Council) in the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Council when Uttarakhand was part of undivided Uttar Pradesh and later as an MLA (Member of Legislative Assembly) in the Uttarakhand Legislative Assembly. Later, he served as an MP (Member of Parliament) in the Rajya Sabha from 2008 to 2014 for Uttarakhand. He also became an MP in the 16th Lok Sabha representing Nainital-Udhamsingh Nagar constituency. This made him a member of both houses of the state legislature and national parliament.

Ingar Axel Harald Ericsson, born on August 31, 1927, and passed away on May 14, 2020, was a Swedish middle-distance runner who focused on the 1500 meters event. He participated in the 1952 and 1956 Summer Olympics. In 1952, he finished eighth place. At the European Championships, he ranked seventh in 1950 and fourth in 1954. Ericsson won the national 1500 meters title three times: in 1952, 1954, and 1955. He also set a new national record in 1956. His job was to be a firefighter.

Television that uses radio waves sent from Earth-based transmitters is called terrestrial television. It's more common in Europe and Latin America, but in the U.S., it’s known as broadcast or over-the-air (OTA) TV. This type of TV is different from satellite, cable, and internet streaming services. Terrestrial TV stations send signals on frequencies between 52 to 600 MHz using VHF and UHF bands. The signal travels by line of sight, so the reception range is limited by the visual horizon. This was the first method for broadcasting TV. The BBC started in 1929, with many radio stations following in 1930. Early systems were not good enough to attract viewers due to low picture quality and mechanical technology. TV became popular after World War II when electronic technology improved picture quality. TV stations worked like radio networks, with local affiliates connected to national networks. Until the 1950s, all TV broadcasts were in black and white. Color TV only came later. Cable TV began in the 1950s but initially just re-broadcasted over-the-air signals. By the 1970s and 1980s, cable became popular in the U.S., leading to fewer people using antennas for terrestrial TV. In 2018, only about 14% of American homes used antennas. However, many other regions still prefer terrestrial TV. As of 2020, it was estimated that at least 1.6 billion people worldwide use this method, with Indonesia having the largest market. By 2019, over-the-top media services, which are streamed via the internet, became a common alternative to terrestrial TV.
Adrienne is a feminine version of the male name Adrien. It means "from the city Hadria."

Daewoo Motors was a South Korean car company that began in 1983 as part of the Daewoo group. In 2001, they sold most of their assets to General Motors due to money problems. After that, it became General Motors' subsidiary. By 2011, Daewoo Motors was replaced by GM Korea.

Nuclear espionage involves sharing state secrets about nuclear weapons with other countries without permission. There have been many known cases of this, as well as suspected ones. Since nuclear weapons are very important state secrets, all countries with such weapons have strict rules against giving away information on how they're designed, how many there are, how they're delivered, and where they're deployed. Countries also limit what they can say publicly about their nuclear weapons through agreements that prevent the spread of these weapons.

Typhoon Lekima was the second strongest tropical storm worldwide in 2013. It was also the twenty-ninth named storm and the eleventh typhoon of that year's season. It became a tropical storm on October 20. On October 22, Lekima intensified into a typhoon and quickly grew stronger due to good weather conditions. On the next day, it reached its strongest point. For over one day, Lekima stayed very strong. Then, starting on October 24, it began to weaken because of stronger winds and changes in the air flow. By October 26, Typhoon Lekima had changed into an extratropical cyclone east of Japan. Even though Lekima was very strong, it didn't cause much damage as it didn't hit any populated areas.

The Adventures of Quentin Durward, known as Quentin Durward, is a 1955 American film made by MGM. Richard Thorpe directed it, and Pandro S. Berman produced it. The story was written by Robert Ardrey, based on Sir Walter Scott's 1823 novel with the same name. This movie starred Robert Taylor and was part of an unofficial trilogy along with Ivanhoe (1952) and Knights of the Round Table (1953). All were made at MGM's British studios near London. The film had a special soundtrack by Bronislau Kaper instead of Miklos Rozsa, who was busy working on other projects. Kay Kendall, a British actress, starred in her first big-budget film. Notable British actors like Robert Morley also appeared in it.

Ilmajoki is a town in Finland's South Ostrobothnia region. It was founded in 1865 and has 12,165 people living there as of February 28, 2017. The town covers 579.79 square kilometers, with 2.89 square kilometers being water. There are about 20 people per square kilometer. Ilmajoki borders four other towns: Isokyrö, Kurikka, Laihia, and Seinäjoki. The town speaks Finnish. Ilmajoki is surrounded by nature with a beautiful view. Kyrönjoki, the largest river in South Ostrobothnia, flows nearby. It has been chosen as one of Finland's national landscapes. In the past year, the population increased by 700 people. One out of every five residents is younger than 14 years old. Ilmajoki’s tax rate is low at 20.24%, making it the lowest in South Ostrobothnia. The town produces more renewable electricity than it uses. Each June, many people come for opera performances by the Ilmajoki Music Festival. There are many historical sites to see. Tero Pitkämäki, an Olympic javelin thrower, and Marko Yli-Hannuksela, a former Finnish wrestler, are from here. Business and entrepreneurship have long traditions in Ilmajoki, with nearly 1,000 companies. The town is often rated as one of the best for businesses. The largest factory in Ilmajoki is Altia’s Koskenkorva plant, which makes ethanol for their clear spirit drink called Koskenkorva or "Kossu." This drink is well-known both in Finland and internationally. There's also a good airport in Rengonkylä, and an important road runs through the town. From Ilmajoki, you can travel 17 km to Seinäjoki, 70 km to Vaasa, 150 km to Tampere, or 360 km to Helsinki.

dhayam is a 2017 Tamil thriller movie made in India. Kannan Rangaswamy wrote and directed it, and A.R.S. Sunder produced it. The entire film was shot inside one room. Santhosh Prathap, Jayakumar, Aanchal Singh, Sandhu Samaira, and Iraa Agarwal are the main actors. Sathish Selvam composed the music, A.Packiaraj did the cinematography, and R.Sudharsan edited it. It was shown in theaters on March 24, 2017.

Mystery Science Theater 3000, often abbreviated to MST3K, is an American comedy TV show created by Joel Hodgson. It’s currently produced by Alternaversal Productions LLC. The show first aired on KTMA-TV in Minneapolis on November 24, 1988. It ran for seven seasons on Comedy Central until it was canceled in 1996. Later, it moved to the Sci-Fi Channel for three more seasons until its cancellation in August 1999. A syndication package called "The Mystery Science Theater Hour" produced in 1993 aired from 1995 onwards. In 2015, Hodgson led a crowdfunded revival with 14 episodes in the show’s eleventh season, first released on Netflix on April 14, 2017. Another six-episode season followed on November 22, 2018. The original series featured Joel Robinson, played by Joel Hodgson, as a janitor stuck on a satellite called "Satellite of Love" with two mad scientists. He had to watch bad movies and use robots to keep himself company and comment on them humorously. Each episode included one movie and sometimes short films at the beginning. The show’s cast changed over time, notably replacing Joel in the fifth season by Mike Nelson. In 2017, a new version of the show was produced with a mostly new cast including Jonah Ray as the new human test subject, Jon Heston. Other characters were played by Felicia Day and Patton Oswalt as "the mads," while Baron Vaughn, Hampton Yount, and Rebecca Hanson voiced Tom Servo, Crow T. Robot, and Gypsy respectively. The original show didn’t get many viewers at first but gained popularity through word-of-mouth among its fans and through syndication and home media releases by Rhino Entertainment. The revived series continues to be popular under Shout! Factory’s ownership with Hodgson’s support. MST3K was named one of Time magazine's 100 best TV shows in 2007, and TV Guide listed it as one of the top cult TV shows. It won a Peabody Award in 1993 and was nominated for two Emmy Awards from 1994 to 1995. The show influenced social television practices, and some former cast members started similar projects like Film Crew and RiffTrax. MST3K also helped bring attention back to older, poorly received movies that had been forgotten. Many of these films are now considered among the worst ever made.

Les sylphides is a short, non-story ballet. It is often seen as the first ballet that focuses only on mood and dance. There is no plot; instead, it features dancing sylphs in white clothes under the moonlight. A man dressed in white tights and a black tunic, possibly representing a poet or young man, also dances. The original choreography was by Michel Fokine. The music comes from Frédéric Chopin, orchestrated by Alexander Glazunov. Some of this music had already been used as a standalone orchestral suite called Chopiniana in 1892. It was first performed to the public in December 1893, conducted by Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov.
Fayette County is named for the Marquis de Lafayette. There are eleven such counties in the United States. The Marquis de Lafayette was a Frenchman who fought in the American Revolution.

John Walton was an Australian actor from 1952 to July 17, 2014. He appeared on stage, TV, and in movies. People remembered him most for being in the TV show "The Young Doctors." He was born in St. Ives, Sydney, Australia.
